(Indeed I fear for you the punishment of a painful day.)

**Fourth commentary:** There are four issues in this verse.

**First:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the chiefs (al-Mala')﴾. Abu Ishaq al-Zajjaj said: *al-Mala'* means the leaders, that is, they are "full" (*maliyyun*) of what they say. This has already been discussed in *al-Baqarah* [[See vol. 3, p. 243]] and elsewhere.

(﴿We see you only as a human being﴾) meaning, a human of Adam's descendants.

(﴿like us﴾) is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (*hal*). *Mithlana* is grammatically a construct with a definite noun, yet it functions as an indefinite, so the nunation is understood as implied. As the poet said [[He is Abu Mihjan al-Thaqafi, and the full line is: "Fair-skinned, whom I have provided for with divorce." *al-Gharirah* means one deceived by an easy life; *matta'ahā* means he gave her what she would enjoy at her divorce.]]:

*O how many a one like you among women is a deceived one*

**Second:** His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And we see none following you except those who are our lowest (*arādhilunā*)﴾. *Arādhil* is the plural of *arādhil*, and *arādhil* is the plural of *radhl*, like *kalb*, *aklub* and *akālib*. It was also said that *arādhil* is the plural of *al-arādhil*, like *asāwid*, the plural of *al-aswad* among snakes. *Al-radhl* means the base person. They meant: those who follow you are our lowly, our fallen, our most despicable. Al-Zajjaj said: they attributed them to weaving, and did not know that crafts have no effect on religious standing. Al-Nahhas said: *al-arādhil* are the poor, those with no lineage to speak of, and those who practice the most menial crafts. In a hadith it is said: "They were weavers and cuppers." This was ignorance on their part, because they reproached the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) for something that carries no fault. The prophets, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon them, are only obligated to bring proofs and signs; they are not obligated to change outward forms and conditions. They are sent to all people. So if the lowly among them embrace Islam, no deficiency reaches them because of that, since they are obliged to accept the Islam of everyone who submits among them.

I say: *al-arādhil* here means the poor and the weak, as Heraclius said to Abu Sufyan: "Did the nobles of the people follow him, or their weak?" He said: "Rather, their weak." He said: "They are the followers of the messengers." Our scholars said: this was because leadership had taken hold of the nobles, because it is hard to be free of it, and because of pride in submitting to others. The poor man is free of those obstacles, so he is quick to respond and submit. This is the common condition of the people of this world.

**Third:** The scholars differed in identifying *al-saflah* (the base, the lowly) in several opinions. Ibn al-Mubarak reported from Sufyan that *al-saflah* are those who *yutaqallisun* [[*al-taqlis*: receiving rulers when they arrive with all kinds of entertainment]] and who come to the doors of judges and rulers seeking testimonies.

Tha'lab reported from Ibn al-A'rabi: *al-saflah* are those who eat the world with their religion [[So in ʿ; the other manuscripts have the singular.]]. It was said to him: "Then who is the basest of the base?" He said: "The one who improves the worldly affairs of others at the cost of his own religion."

Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about the base, and he said: "Those who, when they gather, prevail, and when they scatter, are not recognized."

Malik ibn Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked: "Who are the base?" He said: "The one who insults the Companions."

It was reported from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: *al-arādhilūn* are the weavers and the cuppers.

Yahya ibn Aktham: the tanner and the sweeper, if he is not Arab.

**Fourth:** If a wife says to her husband, "You base one!" and he replies, "If I am of them, then you are divorced," al-Naqqash reported that a man came to al-Tirmidhi and said: "My wife called me 'you base one,' so I said: 'If I am base, then you are divorced.'" Al-Tirmidhi said: "What is your trade?" He said: "A fish seller." He said: "Base, by Allah, base, by Allah."

I say: according to what Ibn al-Mubarak reported from Sufyan, she is not divorced; the same applies according to Malik's view; and according to Ibn al-A'rabi, nothing is incumbent on him.

His saying, exalted is He: (﴿at first sight﴾). That is, at the first appearance of the opinion, while their inner reality is contrary to that. It is said: *bada yabdu* when it appears, as the poet said:

*So today, when they appeared to the onlookers*

The desert is called *bādiyah* because it is apparent. *Badā lī an af'ala kadhā* means a different opinion appeared to me than the first. Al-Azhari said: its meaning is according to the opinion that appears to us. It is also possible that *bādiya al-ra'y* derives from *bada'a yabda'u* with the hamza dropped. Abu Amr made the hamza explicit and read *bādi'a al-ra'y*, meaning "the first opinion," i.e., they followed you when they first began to look, and had they looked deeply and thought carefully, they would not have followed you. The meaning does not differ here whether the hamza is pronounced or dropped. It is in the accusative by omitting *fi* (in), as the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿And Musa chose his people﴾ [[See vol. 7, p. 294.]] [al-A'raf: 155].

(﴿and we see for you no superiority over us﴾) meaning, in following him. This is their denial of his prophethood (ﷺ).

(﴿Rather, we think you are liars﴾) The address is to Nuh and whoever believed with him [[In ʿ and Y: "with him."]].

**Qur'an 11:28–31: Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran)**

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Said he: "O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾, meaning upon certainty. This was said by Abu 'Imran al-Jawni. It was also said that it means upon a miracle, and this meaning has already been discussed in *al-An'am* [[See vol. 6, p. 438.]].

(And has given me mercy from Him) meaning prophethood and messengership, according to Ibn 'Abbas. This mercy is for all creation. It was also said that it means guidance to Allah through proofs, and it was said that it means faith and Islam.

(But it has been made obscure to you) [[The reading of Nafi'.]] meaning the message and the guidance have been made obscure to you, so you did not understand them. One says: "I was blind to such-and-such" (*'amitu 'an kadha*), and "such-and-such was obscure to me" ('amiya 'alayya kadha), meaning I did not understand it. The meaning is: "the mercy became obscure." It was said that this is an inversion (*maqlub*), because mercy cannot be blinded; rather, one is blinded to it. It is like your saying: "I inserted my head into the cap" and "the boot entered my foot." Al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read *fa-'ummiyat* with a *damma* on the *'ayn* and a shadda on the *mim*, in the passive form, meaning that Allah has made it obscure to you (*fa-'ammaha Allahu 'alaykum*). Likewise in the reading of Ubayy: *fa-'ammaha*. This was mentioned by al-Mawardi.

(Shall we compel you to it) It was said that "it" refers to the testimony that there is no god but Allah. It was also said that the pronoun refers to the mercy, and it was said that it refers to the clear evidence. That is: shall we compel you to accept it and make it obligatory upon you? This is an interrogative used in the sense of denial: it is not possible for me to force you to know it. Noah, peace be upon him, intended by this statement to answer them. Al-Kisa'i and al-Farra' related *anulzimukumuha* with the first *mim* sukun-ed for lightness (*takhfif*). Sibawayh permitted the like of this, and he cited the verse [[The line is by Imru' al-Qays. The witness is in the sukun of the *ba'* in the word *ashrab* in the state of raising and in connection. *Ihtaqaba al-ithm* means he bore sin. The *wagil* is one who enters upon a drinking gathering without being invited. He says: it has become lawful for me, so I commit no sin by drinking it, since I have fulfilled my vow concerning it. He had vowed not to drink it until he avenged his father.]]:

*Today I drink, not bearing a sin from Allah, nor being an uninvited intruder.*

Al-Nahhas said: It is also permitted, according to the view of Yunus [outside the Qur'an; the addition is from al-Nahhas], that the pronoun be treated like a noun, as you say: "shall we compel you to that?"

(While you are averse to it) meaning it is not valid for you to accept it while you have aversion toward it. Qatadah said: By Allah, if the Prophet of Allah Noah, peace be upon him, had been able, he would have compelled his people to it, but he did not have that power.

(And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth for it) meaning for the conveying, the calling to Allah, and faith in Him, a reward (*ajran*), that is, (wealth), so that it would be burdensome for you [[From ʿ, K and Y.]].

(My reward is only from Allah) meaning my recompense for conveying the message.

(And I will not drive away those who have believed) They asked him to drive away the lowly people who had believed in him, just as the Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ to drive away the freed slaves and the poor, as has been explained earlier in *al-An'am* [[See vol. 6, p. 431 and what follows.]]. He answered them with his words: (Indeed, they are going to meet their Lord). This may have been said to honour them by their meeting with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it may have been said as a matter of dispute, meaning: if I did that, they would argue against me before Allah, and He would recompense them for their faith and recompense the one who drove them away.

(But I see you as a people who are ignorant) in your belittling of them and your request that they be driven away.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O my people, who would support me against Allah?﴾ al-Farra' said: meaning, who would prevent me from His punishment?

(If I drove them away) meaning for their faith.

(Will you not then remember?) [[The reading of Nafi'.]] The *ta'* has been assimilated into the *dhal* (*idgham*). It is also permissible to delete it, so you say: *tadhakkarun*.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And I do not say to you, "With me are the treasuries of Allah," nor do I know the unseen﴾. He informed them of his humility and lowliness before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that he does not claim what is not his from the treasuries of Allah, which are His bounty upon whomever He wills of His servants, and that he does not know the unseen, because the unseen is known only by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

(Nor do I say that I am an angel) meaning I do not say that my station among people is the station of the angels. The scholars have said: the benefit in this statement is an indication that the angels are superior to the prophets, because of their constancy in obedience and the continuity of their worship until the Day of Resurrection, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all. This meaning has already been discussed in *al-Baqarah* [[See vol. 1, p. 189 and what follows.]].

(Nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon) meaning those whom your eyes regard as worthless and despise. The original form is *tazdariyhum*; the *ha'* and the *mim* were deleted because the phrase is long. The *dal* is substituted from a *ta'*, because the original in *tazdari* is *tazturi*, but the *ta'* is changed to *dal* after a *za'*, because the *za'* is voiced (*majhurah*) and the *ta'* is voiceless (*mahmusah*), so a voiced letter from the same point of articulation was substituted for the *ta'*. It is said: *azraytu 'alayhi* means I blamed him, and *zaraytu 'alayhi* means I belittled him. al-Farra' cited:

*The friend keeps away from him, and his wife belittles him, and the young one repulses him.*

(Allah will not give them any good) meaning your belittling them does not nullify their rewards, nor diminish their recompense.

(Allah knows best what is in their souls) so He will recompense them for it and hold them accountable for it.

(Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers) meaning if I were to say what has been mentioned previously. The word *idhan* here is *mulghah* (cancelled in grammatical function), because it is in the middle of the sentence.

Al-Nahhas said: It is also permitted, according to the view of Yunus [outside the Qur'an; the addition is from al-Nahhas], that the pronoun be treated like a noun, as you say: "shall we compel you to that?"

(While you are averse to it) meaning it is not valid for you to accept it while you have aversion toward it. Qatadah said: By Allah, if the Prophet of Allah Noah, peace be upon him, had been able, he would have compelled his people to it, but he did not have that power.

(And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth for it) meaning for the conveying, the calling to Allah, and faith in Him, a reward (*ajran*), that is, (wealth), so that it would be burdensome for you [[From ʿ, K and Y.]].

(My reward is only from Allah) meaning my recompense for conveying the message.

(And I will not drive away those who have believed) They asked him to drive away the lowly people who had believed in him, just as the Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ to drive away the freed slaves and the poor, as has been explained earlier in *al-An'am* [[See vol. 6, p. 431 and what follows.]]. He answered them with his words: (Indeed, they are going to meet their Lord). This may have been said to honour them by their meeting with Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it may have been said as a matter of dispute, meaning: if I did that, they would argue against me before Allah, and He would recompense them for their faith and recompense the one who drove them away.

(But I see you as a people who are ignorant) in your belittling of them and your request that they be driven away.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O my people, who would support me against Allah?﴾ al-Farra' said: meaning, who would prevent me from His punishment?

(If I drove them away) meaning for their faith.

(Will you not then remember?) [[The reading of Nafi'.]] The *ta'* has been assimilated into the *dhal* (*idgham*). It is also permissible to delete it, so you say: *tadhakkarun*.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And I do not say to you, "With me are the treasuries of Allah," nor do I know the unseen﴾. He informed them of his humility and lowliness before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and that he does not claim what is not his from the treasuries of Allah, which are His bounty upon whomever He wills of His servants, and that he does not know the unseen, because the unseen is known only by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

(Nor do I say that I am an angel) meaning I do not say that my station among people is the station of the angels. The scholars have said: the benefit in this statement is an indication that the angels are superior to the prophets, because of their constancy in obedience and the continuity of their worship until the Day of Resurrection, may the blessings of Allah be upon them all. This meaning has already been discussed in *al-Baqarah* [[See vol. 1, p. 189 and what follows.]].

(Nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon) meaning those whom your eyes regard as worthless and despise. The original form is *tazdariyhum*; the *ha'* and the *mim* were deleted because the phrase is long. The *dal* is substituted from a *ta'*, because the original in *tazdari* is *tazturi*, but the *ta'* is changed to *dal* after a *za'*, because the *za'* is voiced (*majhurah*) and the *ta'* is voiceless (*mahmusah*), so a voiced letter from the same point of articulation was substituted for the *ta'*. It is said: *azraytu 'alayhi* means I blamed him, and *zaraytu 'alayhi* means I belittled him. al-Farra' cited:

*The friend keeps away from him, and his wife belittles him, and the young one repulses him.*

(Allah will not give them any good) meaning your belittling them does not nullify their rewards, nor diminish their recompense.

(Allah knows best what is in their souls) so He will recompense them for it and hold them accountable for it.

(Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers) meaning if I were to say what has been mentioned previously. The word *idhan* here is *mulghah* (cancelled in grammatical function), because it is in the middle of the sentence.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 32–35:

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation."﴾ That is, you argued with us and greatly increased your argument, and you exaggerated in it. In the speech of the Arabs, al-jadal (disputation) means exaggeration in contention. It is derived from al-jadl, which is intense twisting, and the falcon is also called ajdal because of its strength among birds. This meaning has already been discussed in "al-An'am" [[See vol. 7, pp. 77 and 174.]] more fully than this. Ibn Abbas recited "fa-aktharta jadalana" (you multiplied our disputation), as mentioned by al-Nahhas. Disputation in religion is praiseworthy, and for this reason Noah and the prophets argued with their peoples until the truth became manifest. Whoever accepts it succeeds and prospers, and whoever rejects it loses and is ruined. But arguing for other than the truth, until falsehood appears in the form of truth, is blameworthy, and its practitioner is blamed in both abodes.

(So bring us what you threaten us with) That is, the punishment.

(If you are among the truthful) in what you say.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He said, "It is only Allah who will bring it upon you, if He wills.﴾ That is, if He wills to destroy you, He will punish you.

(And you will not escape) That is, you will not get away. It was also said: you will not overcome Him by your multitude, because they were proud of that, for they had filled the earth, plain and mountain, as will be mentioned.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And my advice will not benefit you﴾ That is, my delivery of the message and my striving for your faith.

(If I wished to advise you) That is, because you do not accept advice. The linguistic meaning of nush (advice) has already been explained in "Bara'ah" [[See vol. 8, p. 226 onward.]].

(If Allah wills to misguide you) That is, to lead you astray. This is among the things that prove the falsehood of the doctrine of the Mu'tazilah, the Qadariyyah, and whoever agrees with them, for they claim that Allah the Exalted does not will that the disobedient disobey, that the disbeliever disbelieve, or that the misguided be misguided, and that He does not will that such things occur, while Allah does will it. Allah refuted them with His words: "If Allah wills to misguide you." This meaning has already been discussed in "al-Fatihah" [[See vol. 1, p. 149, and vol. 4, p. 20.]] and elsewhere. They have also contradicted their accursed leader Iblis, as we have explained in "al-A'raf" regarding Allah's misguiding of him, when he said: ﴿Because You have led me astray﴾ [al-A'raf: 16]. They have no escape from the words of Noah, peace be upon him: "If Allah wills to misguide you," for he attributed their misguidance to Allah the Exalted, since He is the Guide and the Misleader, glorified be He above what the deniers and the wrongdoers say, exalted to a great degree. It was also said: "to misguide you" means to destroy you, because misguidance leads to destruction. Al-Tabari said: "yughwiyakum" means He will destroy you with His punishment. It is related from Tayy that "aghwa fulan" means a man became ghawiyan, that is, ill, and "aghwaytuhu" means I destroyed him, and from this comes ﴿So they will meet error﴾ [Maryam: 59].

(He is your Lord) So to Him belongs misguidance, and to Him belongs guidance.

(And to Him you will be returned) A threat and a warning.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ They mean the Prophet ﷺ. Iftara is ifta'ala, that is, he fabricated the Qur'an from his own self, and what he related about Noah and his people, said Muqatil. Ibn Abbas said: it is from the dialogue of Noah with his people, and this is more apparent, because before it and after it there is nothing but mention of Noah and his people, so the address is from them and to them.

(Say, "If I have invented it") That is, if I have fabricated it and made it up, meaning the revelation and the message.

(Then upon me is my crime) That is, upon me is the punishment for my crime; and if I am right in what I say, then upon you is the punishment for your denial of me. Al-ijram is the verbal noun of ajrama, which is committing an evil deed. It was also said: that is, the recompense of my sin and my earning. Jarama and ajrama have the same meaning, according to al-Nahhas and others. The poet said:

A banished one of his tribe and a hostage of a crime,
For what my hand committed and my tongue wrongly uttered.

(al-Lisan) [The verse is by al-Hayrdan al-Sa'di, one of the highwaymen of Banu Sa'd.]

Whoever reads "ajrami" with a fatha on the hamza takes it as the plural of jurm, and al-Nahhas also mentioned this.

(And I am innocent of what you commit) That is, of disbelief and denial.

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 36–37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾. "Annahu" (that it) is in the nominative position, as the subject of what has not had its agent named (ism ma lam yusamma fa'iluhu, the grammatical subject of the passive). It may also be in the accusative position, with the implied construction being: bi-"annahu" (with "annahu"). And "amana" (has believed) is in the accusative position, governed by "yu'minu" (will believe). The meaning of the statement is despair of their faith and the continuation of their disbelief, confirming the descent of the threat upon them. Al-Dahhak said: So he supplicated against them when he was told this, and said: ﴿My Lord, leave not upon the earth from among the disbelievers a single dweller﴾ [Noah: 26], and the two verses. It was also said: a man from the people of Noah carried his son on his shoulder, and when the boy saw Noah he said to his father: "Give me a stone." So he gave him a stone, and he threw it at Noah, peace be upon him, and wounded him. Then God, exalted is He, revealed to him: "That none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they have been doing" — meaning, do not be distressed over their destruction so as to become "ba'is," that is, sorrowful. "Al-bu's" is sorrow, and from it is the saying of the poet:

How many a friend or close companion have I lost,
Yet I was not downcast, though the loss was grievous.

It is said: "ibta'asa al-rajul" when something he dislikes reaches him. "Al-ibti'as" is sorrow accompanied by humility.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes and Our revelation﴾, that is, make the ship so that you and those who believe with you may ride in it. "Bi-a'yunina" means within Our sight and where We can see you. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: with Our guarding you, as one guards whom one sees. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: (with Our protection). The meaning is one, and sight is expressed by "eyes" because seeing occurs through them. The plural "a'yun" may be for majesty, not for multiplicity, as He says: ﴿So excellent are the ones who spread out﴾ [al-Dhariyat/al-Mursalat: 23], "fa-ni'ma al-mahidun," and ﴿And We are its expanders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47]. The meaning of "a'yun" in this verse and others may also return to the meaning of "ayn" (eye), as He said: ﴿and that you may be raised under My eye﴾. All of this is an expression of perception and encompassing, and He, glorified is He, is transcendent above senses, likeness, and modality; there is no lord besides Him. It was also said: the meaning of "bi-a'yunina" is by the eyes of Our angels whom We appointed as watchers over your protection and assistance, so the plural on this reading is on its literal sense of multiplicity. It was said: "bi-a'yunina" means by Our knowledge, as Muqatil said. Al-Dahhak and Sufyan said: "bi-a'yunina" means by Our command. It was said: by Our revelation. It was said: by Our help to you in making it. "Wa-wahyina" means according to what We revealed to you concerning its construction.

(And do not address Me concerning those who did wrong; indeed they are to be drowned.) That is, do not ask for their respite, for I am drowning them.

"Bi-a'yunina" means within Our sight and where We can see you. Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: with Our guarding you, as one guards whom one sees. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: (with Our protection). The meaning is one, and sight is expressed by "eyes" because seeing occurs through them. The plural "a'yun" may be for majesty, not for multiplicity, as He says: ﴿So excellent are the ones who spread out﴾ [al-Dhariyat/al-Mursalat: 23], "fa-ni'ma al-mahidun," and ﴿And We are its expanders﴾ [al-Dhariyat: 47]. The meaning of "a'yun" in this verse and others may also return to the meaning of "ayn" (eye), as He said: ﴿and that you may be raised under My eye﴾. All of this is an expression of perception and encompassing, and He, glorified is He, is transcendent above senses, likeness, and modality; there is no lord besides Him. It was also said: the meaning of "bi-a'yunina" is by the eyes of Our angels whom We appointed as watchers over your protection and assistance, so the plural on this reading is on its literal sense of multiplicity. It was said: "bi-a'yunina" means by Our knowledge, as Muqatil said. Al-Dahhak and Sufyan said: "bi-a'yunina" means by Our command. It was said: by Our revelation. It was said: by Our help to you in making it. "Wa-wahyina" means according to what We revealed to you concerning its construction.

(And do not address Me concerning those who did wrong; indeed they are to be drowned.) That is, do not ask for their respite, for I am drowning them.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he was making the ark﴾, meaning "and he began to make it." Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: When God, glorified and exalted, rescued those among the believers who were in the loins and wombs, God revealed to him: "Verily, none of your people will believe except those who have already believed," and "Make the ark." He said: "My Lord, I am not a carpenter." He said: "Yes, for that is before My eye." So he took the adze and set to work with his hand, and his hand did not err. They passed by him and said: "This one who claims he is a prophet has become a carpenter!" So he made it over forty years.

Al-Tha'labi and Abu Nasr al-Qushayri related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Nuh made the ship in two years. Al-Tha'labi added: "That was because he did not know how to make the ark, so God revealed to him to make it like the breast of a bird (jujuʾ al-ta'ir)." Ka'b said: "He built it in thirty years, and God knows best."

Al-Mahdawi said: It has come in a report that the angels were teaching him how to make it.

They differed concerning its length and breadth. From Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: its length was three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty, and its height thirty cubits, and it was made of teak wood. Likewise al-Kalbi, Qatadah and Ikrimah said: its length was three hundred cubits, and the cubit (dhira') is measured to the shoulder (al-mankib). Salman al-Farisi (said so as well). Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the length of the ship was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its breadth six hundred cubits. Al-Tha'labi related it in his book al-'Ara'is.

Ali ibn Zayd narrated from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said to Isa (peace be upon him): "If only you would send us a man who witnessed the ship, so he could tell us about it." So he set out with them until he reached a mound of earth. He took a handful of that dust and said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the grave of Ka'b ibn Ham ibn Nuh [in al-Tabari, al-Durr al-Manthur and al-Kashshaf, it is as here; in the original it reads 'the grave of Sam ibn Nuh']." He struck the mound with his staff and said: "Rise by God's permission." Then he was standing, shaking the dust from his head, and he had grown grey. Isa said to him: "Is this how you died?" He said: "No, rather I died while young, but I thought the Last Hour had come, so that is why I turned grey." He said: "Tell us about Nuh's ship." He said: "Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its breadth six hundred cubits, and it had three decks: a deck in which were the beasts and wild animals, a deck in which were humans, and a deck in which were the birds." He mentioned the rest of the report, as will come, God willing.

[Editorial note: In al-Bahr it is said: "They differed concerning its shape (in squareness and length), its duration of construction, the place where it was built, and its length and breadth, in conflicting statements none of which is authentic." Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: "Know that these investigations do not please me, for they are matters for which there is absolutely no need to know, and no benefit whatsoever attaches to knowing them."]

Al-Kalbi said, as reported by al-Naqqash: The water entered it to a depth of four cubits. It had three doors: a door for the predators and birds, a door for the wild animals, and a door for men and women. Ibn Abbas made it three levels: the lowest level for the wild animals, predators and beasts; the middle for food and drink; and he himself rode in the upper level, and he carried with him the body of Adam (peace be upon him), placed across between the men and the women; then afterwards he buried it at Bayt al-Maqdis. Iblis was with them in the kawthal.

[Note: The kawthal is the stern of the ship, where the sailors and their goods are. It is said: it is the bilge.]

It was also said: the snake and the scorpion came to board the ship, and Nuh said: "I will not carry you, for you are the cause of harm and affliction." They said: "Carry us, for we guarantee to you that we will not harm anyone who remembers you." So whoever recites, when he fears their harm, ﴿Peace be upon Nuh among all the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79], they will not harm him. Al-Qushayri and others mentioned this.

The hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in al-Tarikh, as a raised (marfu') hadith from the narration of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he reaches the evening: 'May God bless Nuh, and peace be upon Nuh,' a scorpion will not sting him that night."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whenever﴾ is a time adverb (zarf).

(A group of the chiefs of his people passed by him and mocked him.) Al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said: it is said "sakhirtu bihi" and "sakhirtu minhu" (both mean "I mocked him"). Regarding their mockery of him, there are two views. The first: they used to see him building his ship on dry land, so they mocked him and ridiculed him, saying: "O Nuh, after prophethood you have become a carpenter!" The second: when they saw him building the ship, and they had never before witnessed a ship being built, they said: "O Nuh, what are you doing?" He said: "I am building a house that will walk on water." They marvelled at his words and mocked him. Ibn Abbas said: There was no river or sea on earth before the Flood, which is why they mocked him, and the waters of the seas are the remnant of the Flood.

(He said: If you mock us) meaning: for our present action in building the ship.

(then we will mock you) tomorrow, at the time of drowning. The meaning of "mockery" here is "considering you ignorant" (al-istijhal); the sense is: If you consider us ignorant, then we consider you ignorant as you consider us so.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So you will soon know who will be overtaken by a punishment that will disgrace him﴾. This is a threat. "Man" (man) is connected to "fa-sawfa ta'lamun" ("you will soon know"), and "ta'lamun" here is transitive to a direct object (mafʿul), meaning: "you will soon know the one to whom the punishment comes." It is also permissible that "man" is interrogative, meaning: "which of us will be overtaken by the punishment?" It has also been said that "man" is in the nominative position as the subject (mubtada'), with "ya'tihi" as the predicate (khabar), and "yukhzihi" as an adjective (sifa) of "adhab." Al-Kisa'i reported that some people of the Hijaz say "sawfa ta'lamun" (dropping the fa'), and whoever says "sa-ta'lamun" drops both the waw and the fa'. The Kufans report "saf ta'lamun" (dropping the 'ayn), while the Basrans only recognise "sawfa taf'alu" and "sa-taf'alu" as two dialects, neither derived from the other. (And it descends upon him) meaning: it becomes obligatory for him and alights upon him.

(a lasting punishment) meaning: a constant one, referring to the punishment of the Hereafter.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven boiled over﴾. Scholars differed about "the oven" (al-tannur) in seven views:

The first: it is the surface of the earth, for the Arabs call the surface of the earth a tannur. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyaynah, because it was said to him: "When you see the water on the surface of the earth, board the ship, you and those with you."

The second: it is the bread-oven in which bread is baked, which was of stone, and it belonged to Hawwa' until it came to Nuh. It was said to him: "When you see the water gushing forth from the oven, board, you and your companions." God caused water to gush from the oven, and his wife became aware of it and said: "O Nuh, the water has boiled over from the oven!" He said: "The promise of my Lord has come true." This is the view of al-Hasan; Mujahid and Atiyyah also reported it from Ibn Abbas.

The third: it is the place where water gathers in the ship, also from al-Hasan.

The fourth: it is the break of dawn and the light of morning, from the expression "nawwara al-fajr tanwiran" (the dawn lit up), said by Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

The fifth: it is the mosque of Kufa, said also by Ali ibn Abi Talib, and by Mujahid. Mujahid said: "It was the area of the oven in Kufa." He also said: "Nuh built the ship inside the mosque of Kufa, and the oven was on the right of the one entering from the side of Kinda. The gushing of the water from it was a sign for Nuh, and an indication of the destruction of his people." The poet, who is Umayyah, said:

"Their oven boiled over, and water surged,
rising above the mountains until it overtopped them."

The sixth: it is the high parts of the earth and its elevated places, said by Qatadah.

The seventh: it is the spring in the island called "the Spring of the Rose" (Ayn al-Warda), related by Ikrimah. Muqatil said: That oven was the oven of Adam; it was in al-Sham, at a place called "Ayn Warda." Ibn Abbas also said: the oven of Adam boiled over in India.

Al-Nahhas said: These views are not contradictory, because God, mighty and majestic, informed us that the water came from the sky and from the earth. He said: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, and caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 11–12]. So these views converge on the point that this was a sign. "Fawaran" means boiling/bubbling. "Al-tannur" is a non-Arabic word that the Arabs arabicised; its pattern is fa'\"ul (fa''al), since its original form is "tannar," and there is no nun before the ra' in Arabic speech [Note: "Zanara" means he filled it; "tazannara" means he pounded; "al-sanar," with a vowel, means harshness of character; "shanara 'alayhi" means he criticised him]. It has also been said: the meaning of "fara al-tannur" is a figure of speech for the presence of the punishment, like the saying "hamiya al-wati'" (the battle grew hot) when the fighting intensified. "Al-wati'" is the oven. It is also said: "fārat qidr al-qawm" (the people's pot boiled over) when their fighting intensified; their poet said:

"You left your pot with nothing in it,
while the pot of the people is hot and boiling."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We said: Load into it two of each kind﴾, meaning a male and a female, to preserve the root of offspring after the Flood. Hafs read "min kullin zawjayn ithnayn" with tanwin on "kullin", meaning: "from every thing, two pairs." Both readings return to one meaning: [a thing] which has another with it and cannot do without it. For two things are called "a pair" (zawjan), in each pair neither can do without the other. The Arabs call each one of them a "zawj": one says "he has two sandals (zawja na'l)" if he has two sandals; likewise "he has a pair of pigeons (zawja hamam)," and "upon him are a pair of shackles (zawja quyud)." God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. A woman is called the "zawj" of a man, and a man is called her "zawj." It may also be said that two are "a zawj," and the two pairs may mean two kinds or two categories, each kind being called a zawj. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and it causes to grow from every pair a beautiful kind﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], meaning: from every colour and kind. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that Abu Qudama wears
is loved for both of them together."

He meant every kind and colour. "Min kullin zawjayn" is in the accusative position governed by "uhmil" (load). "Ithnayn" is an emphasis (ta'kid).

(And your family) meaning: and load your family.

(except for those against whom the word has already gone forth) "Min" is in the accusative position by way of exception (istithna').

(from among them) meaning: by destruction. This was his son Kan'an and his wife Wa'ila; both were disbelievers.

(and those who believe). Al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: meaning: load whoever believed in me, that is, whoever believed you, so "min" is in the accusative position governed by "uhmil."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 38–40 (part 2 of 2):

(﴿وَمَا آمَنَ مَعَهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلٌ﴾) Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: Eighty people believed from his people, among them three of his sons: Sam, Ham and Yafith, and three of his daughters-in-law (kanaʾin, sing. kunnah [[al-kunnah (with fatha): the wife of a son or of a brother.]]). When they came out of the ship, they built a town, which today is called the Town of the Eighty, in the region of Mosul.

It is related in a report that there were eight souls in the ship: Nuh and his wife other than the one who was punished, his three sons and their wives. This is the view of Qatadah, al-Hakam ibn ʿUtaybah, Ibn Jurayj and Muhammad ibn Kaʿb. Ham had intercourse with his wife in the ship, so Nuh prayed to Allah that his semen be changed, and so he brought forth the Sudan (the black peoples).

ʿAta' said: Nuh invoked against Ham that the hair of his offspring would not exceed their ears, and that wherever his descendants were, they would be slaves to the descendants of Sam and Yafith.

Al-Aʿmash said: They were seven: Nuh, three daughters-in-law and three sons, and he omitted Nuh's wife.

Ibn Ishaq said: They were ten besides their wives: Nuh and his sons Sam, Ham and Yafith, and six people from among those who had believed in him, and all their wives.

"Qalil" (قَلِيلٌ) is in the nominative case as the subject of "amana" (آمَنَ), and it is not permissible to put it in the accusative as an exception, because the sentence before it is not complete. However, the benefit of the inclusion of "illa" (إِلَّا) and "ma" (مَا) is that if you say, "Such-and-such and such-and-such believed with him," it would be possible that others besides them had also believed; but when you bring "ma" and "illa," you affirm it for what follows "illa" and negate it for others.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿We said: Load into it two of each kind﴾, meaning a male and a female, to preserve the root of offspring after the Flood. Hafs read "min kullin zawjayn ithnayn" with tanwin on "kullin", meaning: "from every thing, two pairs." Both readings return to one meaning: [a thing] which has another with it and cannot do without it. For two things are called "a pair" (zawjan), in each pair neither can do without the other. The Arabs call each one of them a "zawj": one says "he has two sandals (zawja na'l)" if he has two sandals; likewise "he has a pair of pigeons (zawja hamam)," and "upon him are a pair of shackles (zawja quyud)." God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And that He created the pairs, the male and the female﴾ [al-Najm: 45]. A woman is called the "zawj" of a man, and a man is called her "zawj." It may also be said that two are "a zawj," and the two pairs may mean two kinds or two categories, each kind being called a zawj. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and it causes to grow from every pair a beautiful kind﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], meaning: from every colour and kind. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that Abu Qudama wears
is loved for both of them together."

He meant every kind and colour. "Min kullin zawjayn" is in the accusative position governed by "uhmil" (load). "Ithnayn" is an emphasis (ta'kid).

(And your family) meaning: and load your family.

(except for those against whom the word has already gone forth) "Min" is in the accusative position by way of exception (istithna').

(from among them) meaning: by destruction. This was his son Kan'an and his wife Wa'ila; both were disbelievers.

(and those who believe). Al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: meaning: load whoever believed in me, that is, whoever believed you, so "min" is in the accusative position governed by "uhmil."

When they came out of the ship, they built a town, which today is called the Town of the Eighty, in the region of Mosul.

ʿAta' said: Nuh invoked against Ham that the hair of his offspring would not exceed their ears, and that wherever his descendants were, they would be slaves to the descendants of Sam and Yafith.

Al-Aʿmash said: They were seven: Nuh, three daughters-in-law and three sons, and he omitted Nuh's wife.

**Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verses 38–40 (part 1 of 2):**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he was making the ark﴾, meaning "and he began to make it." Zayd ibn Aslam said: Nuh (ﷺ) remained for a hundred years planting trees, cutting them, and drying them out, and for a hundred years working them. Ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ibn Ashras, from Malik, who said: "It has reached me that the people of Nuh had exhausted the earth, until they had exhausted the plain and the mountain, so that these could not descend to those, nor those ascend to these." So Nuh remained planting trees for a hundred years for the making of the ship, then he gathered them and dried them for a hundred years, while his people mocked him because of what they saw him doing, until there came about, from God's decree concerning them, what came about. It is also narrated from Amr ibn al-Harith who said: Nuh built his ship in the fields of Damascus, and he cut its timber from Mount Lebanon.

Al-Qadi Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi said: When God, glorified and exalted, rescued those among the believers who were in the loins and wombs, God revealed to him: "Verily, none of your people will believe except those who have already believed," and "Make the ark." He said: "My Lord, I am not a carpenter." He said: "Yes, for that is before My eye." So he took the adze and set to work with his hand, and his hand did not err. They passed by him and said: "This one who claims he is a prophet has become a carpenter!" So he made it over forty years.

Al-Tha'labi and Abu Nasr al-Qushayri related from Ibn Abbas, who said: Nuh made the ship in two years. Al-Tha'labi added: "That was because he did not know how to make the ark, so God revealed to him to make it like the breast of a bird (jujuʾ al-ta'ir)." Ka'b said: "He built it in thirty years, and God knows best."

Al-Mahdawi said: It has come in a report that the angels were teaching him how to make it.

They differed concerning its length and breadth. From Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: its length was three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty, and its height thirty cubits, and it was made of teak wood. Likewise al-Kalbi, Qatadah and Ikrimah said: its length was three hundred cubits, and the cubit (dhira') is measured to the shoulder (al-mankib). Salman al-Farisi (said so as well). Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the length of the ship was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its breadth six hundred cubits. Al-Tha'labi related it in his book al-'Ara'is.

Ali ibn Zayd narrated from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The disciples (al-hawariyyun) said to Isa (peace be upon him): "If only you would send us a man who witnessed the ship, so he could tell us about it." So he set out with them until he reached a mound of earth. He took a handful of that dust and said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "God and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the grave of Ka'b ibn Ham ibn Nuh [in al-Tabari, al-Durr al-Manthur and al-Kashshaf, it is as here; in the original it reads 'the grave of Sam ibn Nuh']." He struck the mound with his staff and said: "Rise by God's permission." Then he was standing, shaking the dust from his head, and he had grown grey. Isa said to him: "Is this how you died?" He said: "No, rather I died while young, but I thought the Last Hour had come, so that is why I turned grey." He said: "Tell us about Nuh's ship." He said: "Its length was one thousand two hundred cubits, and its breadth six hundred cubits, and it had three decks: a deck in which were the beasts and wild animals, a deck in which were humans, and a deck in which were the birds." He mentioned the rest of the report, as will come, God willing.

[Editorial note: In al-Bahr it is said: "They differed concerning its shape (in squareness and length), its duration of construction, the place where it was built, and its length and breadth, in conflicting statements none of which is authentic." Al-Fakhr al-Razi said: "Know that these investigations do not please me, for they are matters for which there is absolutely no need to know, and no benefit whatsoever attaches to knowing them."]

Al-Kalbi said, as reported by al-Naqqash: The water entered it to a depth of four cubits. It had three doors: a door for the predators and birds, a door for the wild animals, and a door for men and women. Ibn Abbas made it three levels: the lowest level for the wild animals, predators and beasts; the middle for food and drink; and he himself rode in the upper level, and he carried with him the body of Adam (peace be upon him), placed across between the men and the women; then afterwards he buried it at Bayt al-Maqdis. Iblis was with them in the kawthal.

[Note: The kawthal is the stern of the ship, where the sailors and their goods are. It is said: it is the bilge.]

It was also said: the snake and the scorpion came to board the ship, and Nuh said: "I will not carry you, for you are the cause of harm and affliction." They said: "Carry us, for we guarantee to you that we will not harm anyone who remembers you." So whoever recites, when he fears their harm, ﴿Peace be upon Nuh among all the worlds﴾ [al-Saffat: 79], they will not harm him. Al-Qushayri and others mentioned this.

The hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned in al-Tarikh, as a raised (marfu') hadith from the narration of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he reaches the evening: 'May God bless Nuh, and peace be upon Nuh,' a scorpion will not sting him that night."

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Whenever﴾ is a time adverb (zarf).

(A group of the chiefs of his people passed by him and mocked him.) Al-Akhfash and al-Kisa'i said: it is said "sakhirtu bihi" and "sakhirtu minhu" (both mean "I mocked him"). Regarding their mockery of him, there are two views. The first: they used to see him building his ship on dry land, so they mocked him and ridiculed him, saying: "O Nuh, after prophethood you have become a carpenter!" The second: when they saw him building the ship, and they had never before witnessed a ship being built, they said: "O Nuh, what are you doing?" He said: "I am building a house that will walk on water." They marvelled at his words and mocked him. Ibn Abbas said: There was no river or sea on earth before the Flood, which is why they mocked him, and the waters of the seas are the remnant of the Flood.

(He said: If you mock us) meaning: for our present action in building the ship.

(then we will mock you) tomorrow, at the time of drowning. The meaning of "mockery" here is "considering you ignorant" (al-istijhal); the sense is: If you consider us ignorant, then we consider you ignorant as you consider us so.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So you will soon know who will be overtaken by a punishment that will disgrace him﴾. This is a threat. "Man" (man) is connected to "fa-sawfa ta'lamun" ("you will soon know"), and "ta'lamun" here is transitive to a direct object (mafʿul), meaning: "you will soon know the one to whom the punishment comes." It is also permissible that "man" is interrogative, meaning: "which of us will be overtaken by the punishment?" It has also been said that "man" is in the nominative position as the subject (mubtada'), with "ya'tihi" as the predicate (khabar), and "yukhzihi" as an adjective (sifa) of "adhab." Al-Kisa'i reported that some people of the Hijaz say "sawfa ta'lamun" (dropping the fa'), and whoever says "sa-ta'lamun" drops both the waw and the fa'. The Kufans report "saf ta'lamun" (dropping the 'ayn), while the Basrans only recognise "sawfa taf'alu" and "sa-taf'alu" as two dialects, neither derived from the other. (And it descends upon him) meaning: it becomes obligatory for him and alights upon him.

(a lasting punishment) meaning: a constant one, referring to the punishment of the Hereafter.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Until, when Our command came and the oven boiled over﴾. Scholars differed about "the oven" (al-tannur) in seven views:

The first: it is the surface of the earth, for the Arabs call the surface of the earth a tannur. This was said by Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah, al-Zuhri and Ibn Uyaynah, because it was said to him: "When you see the water on the surface of the earth, board the ship, you and those with you."

The second: it is the bread-oven in which bread is baked, which was of stone, and it belonged to Hawwa' until it came to Nuh. It was said to him: "When you see the water gushing forth from the oven, board, you and your companions." God caused water to gush from the oven, and his wife became aware of it and said: "O Nuh, the water has boiled over from the oven!" He said: "The promise of my Lord has come true." This is the view of al-Hasan; Mujahid and Atiyyah also reported it from Ibn Abbas.

The third: it is the place where water gathers in the ship, also from al-Hasan.

The fourth: it is the break of dawn and the light of morning, from the expression "nawwara al-fajr tanwiran" (the dawn lit up), said by Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.

The fifth: it is the mosque of Kufa, said also by Ali ibn Abi Talib, and by Mujahid. Mujahid said: "It was the area of the oven in Kufa." He also said: "Nuh built the ship inside the mosque of Kufa, and the oven was on the right of the one entering from the side of Kinda. The gushing of the water from it was a sign for Nuh, and an indication of the destruction of his people." The poet, who is Umayyah, said:

"Their oven boiled over, and water surged,
rising above the mountains until it overtopped them."

The sixth: it is the high parts of the earth and its elevated places, said by Qatadah.

The seventh: it is the spring in the island called "the Spring of the Rose" (Ayn al-Warda), related by Ikrimah. Muqatil said: That oven was the oven of Adam; it was in al-Sham, at a place called "Ayn Warda." Ibn Abbas also said: the oven of Adam boiled over in India.

Al-Nahhas said: These views are not contradictory, because God, mighty and majestic, informed us that the water came from the sky and from the earth. He said: ﴿So We opened the gates of heaven with pouring water, and caused the earth to burst forth with springs﴾ [al-Qamar: 11–12]. So these views converge on the point that this was a sign. "Fawaran" means boiling/bubbling. "Al-tannur" is a non-Arabic word that the Arabs arabicised; its pattern is fa'\"ul (fa''al), since its original form is "tannar," and there is no nun before the ra' in Arabic speech [Note: "Zanara" means he filled it; "tazannara" means he pounded; "al-sanar," with a vowel, means harshness of character; "shanara 'alayhi" means he criticised him]. It has also been said: the meaning of "fara al-tannur" is a figure of speech for the presence of the punishment, like the saying "hamiya al-wati'" (the battle grew hot) when the fighting intensified. "Al-wati'" is the oven. It is also said: "fārat qidr al-qawm" (the people's pot boiled over) when their fighting intensified; their poet said:

"You left your pot with nothing in it,
while the pot of the people is hot and boiling."

It may also be said that two are "a zawj," and the two pairs may mean two kinds or two categories, each kind being called a zawj. God, may He be exalted, said: ﴿and it causes to grow from every pair a beautiful kind﴾ [al-Hajj: 5], meaning: from every colour and kind. Al-A'sha said:

"And every pair of brocade that Abu Qudama wears
is loved for both of them together."

He meant every kind and colour. "Min kullin zawjayn" is in the accusative position governed by "uhmil" (load). "Ithnayn" is an emphasis (ta'kid).

(And your family) meaning: and load your family.

(except for those against whom the word has already gone forth) "Min" is in the accusative position by way of exception (istithna').

(from among them) meaning: by destruction. This was his son Kan'an and his wife Wa'ila; both were disbelievers.

(and those who believe). Al-Dahhak and Ibn Jurayj said: meaning: load whoever believed in me, that is, whoever believed you, so "min" is in the accusative position governed by "uhmil."

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verses 41–44 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And he said, "Embark upon it"﴾. This is a command to board. It may come from Allah the Exalted, or it may be Noah's command to his people. Ruku (riding, boarding) means being raised up over the back of a thing, and it is said: "The debt rode him" (rakibahu al-dayn). The sentence contains an ellipsis, meaning: "Ride the water in the ark." It is also said that the meaning is: "Ride it." The "fi" (in) here is for emphasis, as in His saying: ﴿If you are interpreters of dreams﴾ [Yusuf: 43]. The purpose of "fi" is that they were commanded to be inside its hollow, not on its back.

Ikrimah said: Noah, peace be upon him, boarded the ship on the tenth of Rajab, and the ship came to rest on al-Judi on the tenth of Muharram, which makes six months. Qatadah said: "And he added, and that was the Day of Ashura, so he said to those who were with him: whoever was fasting, let him complete his fast, and whoever was not fasting, let him fast." Al-Tabari (d. 310 AH) mentioned in this regard a hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ): "Noah boarded the ship on the first day of Rajab and fasted the whole month, and the ship sailed with them until the Day of Ashura, when it came to rest on al-Judi, so Noah and those with him fasted it." Al-Tabari also mentioned from Ibn Ishaq what implies that he remained on the water for about a year, and that the ship passed by the House (the Ka'bah) and circled it seven times, and that Allah had lifted it above drowning, so no drowning reached it. Then it went on to Yemen, and returned to al-Judi and came to rest upon it.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿In the name of Allah be its course and its anchorage﴾. The reading of the people of the two sanctuaries (Makkah and Madinah) and the people of Basra is with a dammah on the mim in both words, except for the irregular (shadh) reading. The meaning is: "In the name of Allah is its running and its mooring." So "mujraha" and "mursaha" are in the nominative position as the subject of the sentence. It is permissible for them to be in the accusative position, and the implied sense is: "In the name of Allah at the time of its running," then "waqt" (time) was dropped and "majraha" was put in its place.

Al-A'mash, Hamzah and al-Kisa'i read: "bismillahi majraha" with a fatha on the mim, and "mursaha" with a dammah on the mim. Yahya ibn Isa narrated from al-A'mash, from Yahya ibn Wuthab: "bismillahi majraha wa marsaha" with a fatha on the mim in both, as a verbal noun from "jarat tajri jaryan wa majran" and "rasat rusuwwan wa marsan" when it became firm.

Mujahid, Sulayman ibn Jundub, Asim al-Jahdari and Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read: "bismillahi majraha wa mursaha" as an adjective of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, in the genitive position. It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative position, by supposing an implied subject: i.e. He is its runner and its anchorer. The accusative is also permissible as a circumstantial state.

Al-Dahhak said: When Noah, peace be upon him, said "In the name of Allah be its course," it ran, and when he said "In the name of Allah be its anchorage," it came to rest.

Marwan ibn Salim narrated from Talhah ibn Abdullah ibn Kurayz, from al-Husayn ibn Ali, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "It is a safeguard for my nation from drowning when they board ships, saying: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." ﴿They did not appraise Allah with His true appraisal; and the earth entirely will be His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Glory be to Him, and high is He above what they associate﴾ [Al-Zumar: 67]. "In the name of Allah be its course and its anchorage; indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful." In this verse there is evidence for mentioning the basmalah (the saying "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate") at the beginning of every action, as we explained in the chapter on the basmalah, and praise be to Allah.

﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, i.e. to the people of the ark. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: "When dung and filth increased, Allah revealed to Noah: squeeze the tail of the elephant. So a male pig and a female pig came out of it, and they set about the dung. Noah said: If only I had squeezed the tail of this pig! So he did, and a male mouse and a female mouse came out of it. When they fell, they turned to the ark and its ropes, gnawing at them, and gnawing at the provisions and foodstuffs, until they feared for the ropes of the ark. So Allah revealed to Noah: rub the forehead of the lion, and he rubbed it, and two cats came out of it and ate the mice. When he carried the lion in the ark, he said: O Lord, from where shall I feed it? He said: I will keep it busy. Then fever seized it, and so it has remained feverish forever." Ibn Abbas said: "The first of the animals that Noah carried in the ark was the goose, and the last he carried was the donkey." He said: "Iblis clung to its tail, and its two hands had entered the ark while its two feet were still outside. So the donkey began to struggle and could not enter. Noah cried out to it: Enter, woe to you! It kept struggling, so he said: Enter, woe to you, even if Satan is with you! A phrase slipped from his tongue, so he entered, and Satan leapt and entered too. Then Noah saw him singing in the ark, and said to him: O accursed one, what brought you into my house? He said: You permitted me. So he mentioned it to him, and said: Get up and leave. He said: You have no choice but to carry me with you. So, as they claim, he was on the back of the ark." Noah, peace be upon him, had two shining beads, one in place of the sun and the other in place of the moon. Ibn Abbas said: "One of them was white like the brightness of day, and the other was black like the darkness of night. He would know by them the times of prayer: when it was evening, the blackness of this one prevailed over the whiteness of that one, and when it was morning, the whiteness of this one prevailed over the blackness of that one, according to the measure of the hours."

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains﴾. "Mawj" is the plural of "mawjah", which is that part of a large body of water that rises when the wind becomes violent. The "ka" (like) is for comparison, and it is in the genitive position as an adjective of "mawj" (waves). It is mentioned in the tafsir (exegesis) that the water rose above everything by fifteen cubits.

﴿And Noah called out to his son﴾. It was said: he was a disbeliever, and his name was Kan'an. It was also said: his name was Yam. It is permissible, according to the view of Sibawayh, that the phrase "wa nada Nuhun ibnahu" (and Noah called out to his son) be recited with the waw dropped from "ibnahu" in pronunciation. He cited (as evidence) the line of poetry:

"He has a roar as if it were the voice of a driver, when he seeks his mate or his mount."

As for "wa nada Nuhun ibnah wa kana" (the reading with the alif), it is an irregular reading (shadh), which is transmitted from Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah honour his face, and Urwah ibn al-Zubayr. Abu Hatim claimed that it is permissible on the basis that he means "ibnaha" (her son), dropping the alif, just as you say "ibnahu" and drop the waw. Al-Nahhas said: What Abu Hatim said is not permissible according to the school of Sibawayh, because the alif is light and so it cannot be dropped, whereas the waw is heavy and may be dropped.

﴿And he was apart﴾, i.e. from his father's religion. It is also said: apart from the ship. It is also said: Noah did not know that his son was a disbeliever, and he thought he was a believer, and for this reason he said to him: ﴿and do not be with the disbelievers﴾, as will come. This call took place before the people were certain of drowning and before they saw despair, rather it was at the very beginning, when the oven boiled over and the sign appeared to Noah.

Asim read: "Ya bunayya irkab ma'anā" with a fatha on the ya, while the rest read it with a kasra. The original form of "ya bunayya" is with three ya's: the ya of diminutive, the ya of the verb, and the ya of possession. The ya of diminutive was merged into the final consonant of the verb, the final letter of the verb was given a kasra because of the ya of possession, and the ya of possession was dropped because it came in the position of tanwin, or because it and the ra' were both quiescent in this position. This is the origin of the reading of those who used kasra on the ya. It is also the origin of the reading of those who used fatha, because he changed the ya of possession into an alif for the lightness of the alif, then dropped the alif because it was a substitute for a dropped letter, or because it and the ra' were quiescent.

Al-Nahhas said: As for Asim's reading, it is problematic. Abu Hatim said: He means "ya bunayyah", then it is dropped. Al-Nahhas said: I saw Ali ibn Sulayman holding that this is not permissible, because the alif is light. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: I do not know of any grammarian who permitted speaking in this way except Abu Ishaq, who claimed that the fatha is on two grounds and the kasra on two grounds. The fatha is on the basis that the ya is changed into an alif, as Allah the Mighty and Majestic says in report: ﴿O woe to me!﴾ [Hud: 72], and as the poet said:

"How strange it is about her saddle that carries"

So he means "ya bunaya", then the alif is dropped to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters, just as you say "jaa'ni abdā Allah" in the dual. The other ground is that the alif is dropped because the vocative is a place for dropping. The kasra is on the basis that the ya is dropped for the vocative. The other ground is that it is dropped to avoid the meeting of two quiescent letters.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿He said: I will betake myself﴾, i.e. I will return and join myself.

﴿to a mountain that will protect me﴾, i.e. will prevent me, ﴿from the water, so I will not drown﴾.

﴿He said: There is no protector today from the command of Allah﴾, i.e. no preventer, for it is a day on which punishment has been decreed for the disbelievers. "Asima" is in the accusative as an exception of negation (tabri'a). It is also permissible to read "la 'asima al-yawm," with "la" meaning "laysa" (is not).

﴿except for him on whom He has mercy﴾ is in the accusative position as an exception that is not from the first part, i.e. but whomever Allah has mercy upon, He protects. Al-Zajjaj said: It is also permissible for it to be in the nominative position, on the basis that "'asim" means "ma'sum" (protected), like His saying: ﴿from a gushing fluid﴾ [Al-Tariq: 6], i.e. "mafquq" (poured forth). On this view the exception is connected. A poet said:

"Slow in rising, gentle in speech, my heart has become captivated by her"

i.e. "maftun" (captivated). Another said [the verse is by al-Hutay'ah, satirizing al-Zibriqan]:

"Leave off noble deeds, do not rise to pursue them, and sit, for you are the one who eats and clothes"

i.e. "al-matu'um al-maksu" (the one who is fed and clothed). Al-Nahhas said: Among the best that has been said about this is that "min" is in the nominative position, meaning: no one protects today from the command of Allah except the Merciful, i.e. except Allah. This is the view chosen by al-Tabari. What makes this good is that you have not made "'asim" mean "ma'sum", so as to take it out of its usual sense, nor "innahu" mean "lakin" (but).

﴿And the wave came between them﴾, meaning between Noah and his son.

﴿so he was among the drowned﴾. It is said: He was riding a horse that had grown proud of itself and was pleased with it. When he saw the water, he came and said: O father, the oven has boiled over! His father said to him: "O my son, board with us!" But before the exchange was finished, a great wave came and seized him, together with his horse, and he was cut off from Noah, and so he drowned. It is also said: He built for himself a house of glass in which he would shelter from the water. When the oven boiled over, he entered it and shut it from the inside, and he kept defecating and urinating in it until he drowned in that. It is also said: The mountain to which he betook himself was Mount Sinai (Tur Sina').

**Al-Qurtubi's commentary (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 11, verses 41–44 (part 2 of 3)**

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it was said: O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold your rain.﴾ This is a figurative usage (majaz), because the earth is lifeless (mawat). It has also been said that understanding was placed in them by which they could discern. Whoever said that it is figurative said: "If the speech of the Arabs and the non-Arabs were searched, nothing like this verse would be found, for its fine composition, the eloquence of its arrangement, and the meanings it contains."

There is a report: "Indeed, God, Exalted is He, does not leave the earth without rain for a year or two. Rain never descended from the sky except under the protection of an angel assigned to it, except for the water of the Flood, for something of it went out that the angel did not guard." This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, when the water rose high, We carried you in the sailing ship﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11]. [See vol. 18, p. 262.] The ship then sailed with them until the matter reached its end. God commanded the water pouring from the sky to stop, and God commanded the earth to swallow.

It is said: *bala'a al-ma'a yabla'uhu* (he swallowed the water), like *mana'a yamna'u*, and *bali'a yabla'u* (with the vowel pattern) like *hamida yahmadu*. These are two dialects, related by al-Kisa'i and al-Farra'. Al-Balu'ah (the sink-hole/drain) is the place that drinks the water.

Ibn al-Arabi said: "The two waters met upon a decreed matter: what was in the earth and what had descended from the sky. God commanded what had descended from the sky to withhold, so the earth did not absorb a single drop from it. He commanded the earth to swallow only what had come out of it." This is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it was said: O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold your rain, and the water subsided﴾.

It has also been said: God distinguished between the two waters. What was from the water of the earth, He commanded it, and it swallowed it, and the water of the sky became seas.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And the water subsided﴾, i.e., decreased. It is said: *ghaḍa al-shay'* (the thing subsided) and *ghaḍtuhu ana* (I caused it to subside), just as it is said: *naqasa bi-nafsihi* (it decreased by itself) and *naqasahu ghayruhu* (another decreased it). It is permissible to read *ghīḍa* with a *ḍamma* on the *ghayn* [i.e., with the kasra pronounced with a hint of ḍamma].

﴿And the matter was decided﴾, i.e., it was made firm and completed, meaning the people of Nuh were destroyed completely and thoroughly. It is said that God caused their wombs, i.e., the wombs of their women, to become barren forty years before the drowning, so that no child was among those who perished. The correct view, however, is that He destroyed the young children by the Flood, just as the birds and beasts perished. The drowning was not a punishment for the children, the animals, and the birds; rather, they died at their appointed times.

It is reported that when the water rose in the streets, a mother feared for her child, whom she loved intensely, so she went out with him to the mountain until the water reached a third of it. When the water reached her, she went up until it reached two-thirds of it. When the water reached her, she climbed to the top of the mountain. When the water reached her neck, she raised her hands with her son until the water carried them both away. Had God shown mercy to any of them, He would have shown mercy to the mother of the child.

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And it came to rest on al-Judi, and it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾, i.e., destruction for them. Al-Judi is a mountain near Mosul. The ship came to rest upon it on the tenth of Muharram, the day of 'Ashura'. Nuh fasted, and he commanded everyone with him, of people, wild animals, birds, beasts, and others, to fast as well, in gratitude to God, Exalted is He. This meaning has already been mentioned earlier. It has also been said that this was on a Friday.

It is narrated that God, Exalted is He, revealed to the mountains that the ship would settle upon one of them. So they grew tall, but al-Judi did not grow tall, out of humility before God. Thus the ship came to rest upon it, and its planks remained upon it. In a hadith, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, some of it remained, which the earliest of this ummah reached."

Mujahid said: The mountains rose high and grew tall lest the drowning reach them, and the water rose above them fifteen cubits. Al-Judi lowered itself and humbled itself to the command of God, Exalted is He, so it did not drown, and the ship came to rest upon it.

It has also been said that *al-Judi* is the name of every mountain. From this is the saying of Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl: [The poet is named in *al-Lisan* as Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt, while in *Mu'jam al-Buldan* it is said to be by Zayd ibn 'Amr, or it is said to be by Waraqah ibn Nawfal. In one manuscript the word reads *al-jamad* (in the plural form of *khadim*), and this is probably closer to correct.]

*Glory be to Him, then again glory, returning to Him,*
*And before us al-Judi and the rocks glorified Him.*

It is also said that al-Judi is one of the mountains of Paradise, and for this reason the ship came to rest upon it. It is said: God honored three mountains with three men: al-Judi with Nuh, Tur Sinai with Musa, and Hira' with Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of God be upon them all.

**Issue:** When al-Judi humbled itself and submitted, it was exalted, and when the others rose up and exalted themselves, they were humiliated. This is the way of God with His creation: He raises those who are humble, and He lowers those who are arrogant. The poet has indeed spoken well:

*When necks are humbled in submission*
*Toward You from us, their honor lies in their humility.*

In the Sahih of al-Bukhari and Muslim, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: The she-camel of the Prophet (ﷺ) was called al-'Adba', and no animal could outrun her. A Bedouin came on a young camel of his and outran her. This weighed heavily on the Muslims, and they said, "al-'Adba' has been outrun!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "It is indeed a right upon Allah that He raises nothing of this world except that He brings it low."

Muslim also related, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Charity does not decrease wealth, Allah does not increase a servant through pardon except in honour, and no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him."

He (ﷺ) also said: "Allah has revealed to me that you should be humble, so that no one oppresses another and no one boasts over another." Al-Bukhari transmitted it.

Masalah (a point of discussion): In it we mention part of the story of Noah with his people and some account of the Ark.

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in his History, on the authority of al-Hasan, that Noah was the first messenger whom Allah sent to the people of the earth. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And We sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them a thousand years less fifty years﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 14]. [See vol. 13, p. 332.]

Wickedness had multiplied among them, the tyrants had increased, and they had become excessively arrogant. Noah would call them night and day, secretly and openly. He was patient and forbearing, and no prophet suffered more than what Noah suffered. They would come to him, choke him until he was left half-dead, beat him in their gatherings, and drive him away. He would not invoke a curse upon those who harmed him but would call them and say: "My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know." This only increased their flight from him, to the extent that when he spoke to one of them, that man would wrap his head in his garment and put his two fingers in his ears so that he would not hear any of his words. This is the meaning of His words: ﴿And every time I call them, that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and draw their garments over themselves﴾ [Nuh: 7]. [See vol. 18, p. 300.]

Mujahid and Ubayd ibn 'Umayr said: They would beat him until he fainted, and when he recovered he would say: "My Lord, forgive my people, for they do not know."

Ibn 'Abbas said: Noah would be beaten, then wrapped in felt and thrown into his house, and they thought he had died. Then he would come out and call them again. Until, when he despaired of the faith of his people, a man came to him with his son, who was leaning on a staff. The man said: "O my son, look at this old man, do not let him deceive you." The son said: "O father, give me the staff." So he gave it to him. He took the staff and said: "Put me on the ground." He put him down, and he walked toward Noah with the staff and struck him, wounding him in the head with a serious wound that drew blood. Noah said: "My Lord, You see what Your servants do to me. If there is any good in Your servants, then guide them. If not, then grant me patience until You judge, and You are the best of judges." Allah revealed to him and made him despair of the faith of his people, and informed him that no believer remained in the loins of men or in the wombs of women. He said: "And it was revealed to Noah that none of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not be distressed by what they have been doing" [Hud: 36], meaning: do not grieve over them. "And build the ship under Our eyes and Our revelation" [Hud: 37]. He said: "My Lord, where is the timber?" He said: "Plant trees." So he planted teak for twenty years, and he stopped calling them, and they stopped mocking him. When the trees matured, his Lord commanded him, and he cut them down and dried them. He said: "My Lord, how should I build this house?" He said: "Make it in three forms: its head like the head of a cock, its breast like the breast of a bird, and its tail like the tail of a cock. Make it closed, with doors in its side, and fasten it with dusur," meaning iron nails. Allah sent Gabriel, who taught him the craft of the ship, and his hand did not err.

Ibn 'Abbas said: The home of Noah, peace be upon him, was Damascus, and he built his ship from Lebanese wood between Zamzam and the Rukn and the Maqam. When it was completed, he loaded into it the predators and the animals through the first door, placed the wild beasts and birds in the second door, and sealed them. He placed the sons of Adam, forty men and forty women, in the upper door and sealed it upon them. He also put the ants with him in the upper door, because of their weakness, so that the animals would not trample them.

al-Zuhri said: Allah, mighty and majestic, sent a wind, and from every pair two were brought to him: from the predators, the birds, the wild beasts, and the cattle.

Ja'far ibn Muhammad said: Allah sent Gabriel, who gathered them, and he struck the pairs with his two hands, so that his right hand fell on the male and his left on the female, and he would bring them into the ship.

Zayd ibn Thabit said: The female goat was difficult for Noah to bring into the ship, so he pushed her by her tail, and her tail was broken and became bent, and her private parts became visible. The ewe then walked in, and he rubbed her tail, so her private parts were covered.

Ishaq said: A man of knowledge informed us that Noah carried the people of the ship and placed in it two of every kind, and he took two hoopoes. The female hoopoe died in the ship before the earth appeared. The male hoopoe carried her and went around the world seeking a place for her, but he found no clay or soil. His Lord had mercy on him, and he dug a grave for her in his nape and buried her there. That feathered protrusion on the nape of the hoopoe is the place of the grave, and that is why the napes of hoopoes protrude.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The cargo Noah carried with him in the ship included all kinds of trees, and the 'ajwa date of Paradise was with Noah in the ship."

The author of the book "al-'Arus" and others mentioned that when Noah, peace be upon him, wanted to send someone to bring him news of the earth, the hen said: "I will go." So he took her, sealed her wing, and said to her: "You are sealed with my seal; never fly. My community will benefit from you." Then he sent the raven, which found a carcass and landed upon it and was detained. So he cursed it, and that is why it is killed in the sacred and non-sacred areas alike, and he invoked fear upon it, which is why it does not become familiar with houses. Then he sent the dove, which found no resting place, so it landed on a tree in the land of Sinai [in one manuscript: Saba'; in another: Sa'ba'] and carried an olive leaf and returned to Noah. He knew that she had not been able to settle on the earth. Then he sent her again, and she flew until she landed in the valley of the Sacred House, where the water had receded from the places of the Ka'bah. Its clay was red, so her legs were dyed.
