Evidence for this is His words, "and do not be among the disbelievers," meaning do not be among those who are not of them, because in Noah's opinion his son was a believer. Noah would not have said to his Lord, "Indeed my son is of my family," unless he believed this was so, since it is impossible that he would ask for the destruction of the disbelievers and then ask for the salvation of some of them. His son was concealing disbelief and showing faith. So Allah informed Noah of what He alone possesses of the knowledge of the unseen, meaning: I know about your son's condition what you do not know. Al-Hasan said: he was a hypocrite, and that is why Noah felt entitled to call out to him. It is also reported from him: he was the son of his wife. The evidence for this is the reading of ʿAlī: "And Noah called out to her son."

"﴿And You are the most just of judges﴾", a subject and predicate, meaning: You judged that one people would be saved and another people would be drowned.

**Second issue**: His words, "﴿He said: O Noah, indeed he is not of your family﴾", meaning not of your family whom I promised to save. This was said by Saʿid ibn Jubayr. The majority said: he is not of your religious community or of your allegiance, so this is an ellipsis of a noun (muḍāf). This shows that the ruling of agreement in religion is stronger than the ruling of kinship.

"﴿Indeed he is one whose deed is not righteous﴾". Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUrwa, ʿIkrima, Yaʿqūb and al-Kisāʾī read "innahu ʿamila ghayra ṣāliḥin" (he did an unrighteous deed), meaning of disbelief and denial. Abū ʿUbayd preferred this reading. The rest read "ʿamalun" (a deed), meaning: your son is one who does an unrighteous deed, so the noun (muḍāf) is omitted. This was said by al-Zajjāj and others. He said [the line is by al-Khansāʾ, describing a she-camel whose young has gone from her, from an elegy for her brother Ṣakhr]:

"She grazes as she grazed, until when she remembers... it is only coming and going."

That is, she is one who comes and goes. This view and the preceding one return to a single meaning. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the request, meaning: your request to Me that I save him is an unrighteous deed. This was said by Qatada. Al-Hasan said: the meaning of "an unrighteous deed" is that he was born on his bed but was not his son, and was the child of an illegitimate union. Mujāhid also said this. Qatada said: I asked al-Hasan about him, and he said: "By Allah, he was not his son." I said: Allah reported that Noah said, "Indeed my son is of my family," and he said: he did not say "of me." This is a sign that he was the son of his wife from another husband. I said to him: Allah related that Noah said, "Indeed my son is of my family," and "and Noah called out to his son." The People of the Two Books do not disagree that he was his son. Al-Hasan said: and who takes his religion from the People of the Book? They are liars. He recited: "﴿so they both betrayed them﴾" (66:10). Ibn Jurayj said: he called out to him while thinking he was his son, since he had been born on his bed, but his wife had betrayed him in that, and that is why Allah said, "so they both betrayed them." Ibn ʿAbbās said: no wife of a prophet ever committed adultery, and he was his son by his loins. Likewise said al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿIkrima, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Maymūn ibn Mihrān and others, that he was his son by his loins. It was said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr: Noah says, "Indeed my son is of my family." Was he of his family? Was he his son? He glorified Allah at length, then said: there is no god but Allah! Allah tells Muḥammad (ﷺ) that he was his son, and you say he was not his son! Yes, he was his son, but he opposed him in intention, deed and religion. That is why Allah said, "Indeed he is not of your family." This is the correct view on the matter, if Allah wills, because of the greatness of the one who said it. His words "indeed he is not of your family" do not negate that he was his son. As for His words, "﴿so they both betrayed them﴾" (66:10), this means in religion, not in the marriage bed. The wife used to tell people that he was mad. She said to him: Will your Lord not help you? He said to her: Yes. She said: When? He said: When the oven boils over. So she went out and said to her people: O people, by Allah he is indeed mad. He claims that his Lord will not help him unless this oven boils over. That was her betrayal. The other betrayal was that she used to point out guests to the people, as will come, if Allah wills. And Allah knows best. It was also said: a child may be called a deed just as it is called an earning. This is in the report: "Your children are from your earnings." Al-Qushayrī mentioned this.

**Third issue**: In this verse there is consolation for people concerning the corruption of their children, even if they are righteous. It is reported that the son of Mālik ibn Anas came down from above with a pigeon covering him. Mālik knew that people had understood him, so he said: the manners are the manners of Allah, not the manners of fathers and mothers, and the good is the good of Allah, not the good of fathers and mothers. This verse also shows that a son is included in "family" linguistically and in law, and is among the people of the household. So whoever bequeaths to his family, his son is included, and whoever lives in his house and is under his care. Allah said in another verse: "﴿And Noah had called to Us, and how excellent are the Responders. And We saved him and his family from the great distress﴾" (37:75–76). So He named all whom his house contained as his family.

**Fourth issue**: The verse indicates, according to the view of al-Hasan, Mujāhid and others, that the child belongs to the bed. That is why Noah said what he said, taking the apparent meaning of the bed. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār that he heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say: we see that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged that the child belongs to the bed only because of the son of Noah (peace be upon him). Abū ʿUmar mentioned this in the book *al-Tamhīd*. In the sound ḥadīth from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone," meaning disappointment. It was also said: stoning with stones. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr read: "And Noah called out to her son," meaning the son of his wife. This is the explanation of the earlier reading attributed to him and to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. It is evidence for al-Hasan and Mujāhid, but it is an irregular reading (shādh), so we do not abandon the agreed reading for its sake. And Allah knows best.

**Fifth issue**: His words, "﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾", meaning I forbid you from this request and warn you lest you be one, or lest you dislike being among the ignorant, that is, the sinners. From the same root is His words, "﴿Allah admonishes you never to return to the like of it﴾" (24:17), meaning Allah warns you and forbids you. It was also said: the meaning is "I raise you up so that you are not among the ignorant." Ibn al-ʿArabī said: this is an addition from Allah and an admonition by which He raises Noah above the station of the ignorant and elevates him to the station of the scholars and those who know. So Noah said: "﴿My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge﴾" (11:47). These are the sins of the prophets (peace be upon them), and the gratitude owed to Allah is humility and modesty before Him.

"﴿And unless You forgive me﴾", for what slipped from me of the request.

"﴿and have mercy upon me﴾", meaning by repentance.

"﴿I would be among the losers﴾", meaning in deeds. Then He said: "﴿O Noah, descend in peace from Us﴾" (11:48).

The majority said: he is not of your religious community or of your allegiance, so this is an ellipsis of a noun (muḍāf). This shows that the ruling of agreement in religion is stronger than the ruling of kinship.

"﴿Indeed he is one whose deed is not righteous﴾". Ibn ʿAbbās, ʿUrwa, ʿIkrima, Yaʿqūb and al-Kisāʾī read "innahu ʿamila ghayra ṣāliḥin" (he did an unrighteous deed), meaning of disbelief and denial. Abū ʿUbayd preferred this reading. The rest read "ʿamalun" (a deed), meaning: your son is one who does an unrighteous deed, so the noun (muḍāf) is omitted. This was said by al-Zajjāj and others. He said [the line is by al-Khansāʾ, describing a she-camel whose young has gone from her, from an elegy for her brother Ṣakhr]:

"She grazes as she grazed, until when she remembers... it is only coming and going."

That is, she is one who comes and goes. This view and the preceding one return to a single meaning. It is also possible that the pronoun refers to the request, meaning: your request to Me that I save him is an unrighteous deed. This was said by Qatada. Al-Hasan said: the meaning of "an unrighteous deed" is that he was born on his bed but was not his son, and was the child of an illegitimate union. Mujāhid also said this. Qatada said: I asked al-Hasan about him, and he said: "By Allah, he was not his son." I said: Allah reported that Noah said, "Indeed my son is of my family," and he said: he did not say "of me." This is a sign that he was the son of his wife from another husband. I said to him: Allah related that Noah said, "Indeed my son is of my family," and "and Noah called out to his son." The People of the Two Books do not disagree that he was his son. Al-Hasan said: and who takes his religion from the People of the Book? They are liars. He recited: "﴿so they both betrayed them﴾" (66:10). Ibn Jurayj said: he called out to him while thinking he was his son, since he had been born on his bed, but his wife had betrayed him in that, and that is why Allah said, "so they both betrayed them." Ibn ʿAbbās said: no wife of a prophet ever committed adultery, and he was his son by his loins. Likewise said al-Ḍaḥḥāk, ʿIkrima, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Maymūn ibn Mihrān and others, that he was his son by his loins. It was said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr: Noah says, "Indeed my son is of my family." Was he of his family? Was he his son? He glorified Allah at length, then said: there is no god but Allah! Allah tells Muḥammad (ﷺ) that he was his son, and you say he was not his son! Yes, he was his son, but he opposed him in intention, deed and religion. That is why Allah said, "Indeed he is not of your family." This is the correct view on the matter, if Allah wills, because of the greatness of the one who said it. His words "indeed he is not of your family" do not negate that he was his son. As for His words, "﴿so they both betrayed them﴾" (66:10), this means in religion, not in the marriage bed. The wife used to tell people that he was mad. She said to him: Will your Lord not help you? He said to her: Yes. She said: When? He said: When the oven boils over. So she went out and said to her people: O people, by Allah he is indeed mad. He claims that his Lord will not help him unless this oven boils over. That was her betrayal. The other betrayal was that she used to point out guests to the people, as will come, if Allah wills. And Allah knows best. It was also said: a child may be called a deed just as it is called an earning. This is in the report: "Your children are from your earnings." Al-Qushayrī mentioned this.

**Third issue**: In this verse there is consolation for people concerning the corruption of their children, even if they are righteous. It is reported that the son of Mālik ibn Anas came down from above with a pigeon covering him. Mālik knew that people had understood him, so he said: the manners are the manners of Allah, not the manners of fathers and mothers, and the good is the good of Allah, not the good of fathers and mothers. This verse also shows that a son is included in "family" linguistically and in law, and is among the people of the household. So whoever bequeaths to his family, his son is included, and whoever lives in his house and is under his care. Allah said in another verse: "﴿And Noah had called to Us, and how excellent are the Responders. And We saved him and his family from the great distress﴾" (37:75–76). So He named all whom his house contained as his family.

**Fourth issue**: The verse indicates, according to the view of al-Hasan, Mujāhid and others, that the child belongs to the bed. That is why Noah said what he said, taking the apparent meaning of the bed. Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna narrated from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār that he heard ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr say: we see that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) judged that the child belongs to the bed only because of the son of Noah (peace be upon him). Abū ʿUmar mentioned this in the book *al-Tamhīd*. In the sound ḥadīth from the Prophet (ﷺ) he said: "The child belongs to the bed, and for the adulterer is the stone," meaning disappointment. It was also said: stoning with stones. ʿUrwa ibn al-Zubayr read: "And Noah called out to her son," meaning the son of his wife. This is the explanation of the earlier reading attributed to him and to ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him. It is evidence for al-Hasan and Mujāhid, but it is an irregular reading (shādh), so we do not abandon the agreed reading for its sake. And Allah knows best.

**Fifth issue**: His words, "﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾", meaning I forbid you from this request and warn you lest you be one, or lest you dislike being among the ignorant, that is, the sinners. From the same root is His words, "﴿Allah admonishes you never to return to the like of it﴾" (24:17), meaning Allah warns you and forbids you. It was also said: the meaning is "I raise you up so that you are not among the ignorant." Ibn al-ʿArabī said: this is an addition from Allah and an admonition by which He raises Noah above the station of the ignorant and elevates him to the station of the scholars and those who know. So Noah said: "﴿My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You from asking You about that of which I have no knowledge﴾" (11:47). These are the sins of the prophets (peace be upon them), and the gratitude owed to Allah is humility and modesty before Him.

"﴿And unless You forgive me﴾", for what slipped from me of the request.

"﴿and have mercy upon me﴾", meaning by repentance.

"﴿I would be among the losers﴾", meaning in deeds. Then He said: "﴿O Noah, descend in peace from Us﴾" (11:48).

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 48:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿It was said: "O Noah, descend with peace from Us"﴾ — that is, the angels said to him [[From ʿ and W.]], or Allah, exalted is He, said to him: "Descend from the ship to the earth," or "from the mountain to the earth," for the water had been swallowed up and had dried up. "With peace from Us" means with safety and security. It was also said: with a greeting.

(And blessings upon you) means lasting bounties. It is derived from the kneeling of the camel (burūk al-jamal), which is its settling and remaining in place. From it comes al-barakah (blessing), because water settles and remains in it. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Noah is the lesser Adam, so all creation now descends from his offspring, and there were no men or women in the ship with him except those who were of his descendants, according to the statement of Qatadah and others, as has already been mentioned. In the revelation: ﴿And We made his descendants the survivors﴾ [[See vol. 15, p. 89.]] [al-Saffat: 77].

(And upon nations among those with you) It was said: every believer until the Day of Resurrection is included in this. And included in His saying (and nations We will give enjoyment to, then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment) is every disbeliever until the Day of Resurrection, as narrated from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb. The implied reading according to this is: "and upon the descendants of nations among those with you, and the descendants of nations We will give enjoyment to." It was also said: "min" is partitive, and it may be for explaining the kind. "Wa-umamun sanumattiʿuhum" — the word "umamun" is in the nominative (irtafaʿa), in the sense of "and there will be nations." Al-Akhfash Saʿid said: just as you say, "I spoke to Zayd while ʿAmr is sitting." Al-Farra' permitted, outside of recitation, "wa-umaman," with the implied meaning: "and We will give enjoyment to nations." "ʿAla" was repeated with "umam" because it is coordinated with the kaf in "ʿalayka," which is a pronoun in the genitive case, and one does not coordinate upon a pronoun in the genitive except by repeating the preposition, according to the view of Sibawayh and others. This has been fully explained earlier in (al-Nisa') [[See vol. 5, p. 2 and following.]] in His saying: ﴿And fear Allah, by whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [al-Nisa': 1] with the genitive case.

The bā' in His saying "bi-salamin" is connected to an omitted element, because it is in the position of a circumstantial clause (ḥāl), meaning: "descend greeted with peace upon you." And "minna" is in the genitive position, connected to an omitted element, because it is an attribute of "al-barakat." "ʿAla umamin" is connected to what "ʿalayka" is connected to, because it was repeated on account of the element coordinated with the kaf. And "min" in His saying "mimman maʿaka" is connected to an omitted element, because it is in the genitive position as an attribute of "umam." And "maʿaka" is connected to an omitted verb, because it is the relative clause (ṣilah) of "man," meaning: "of those who settled with you, or believed with you, or rode with you."

Commentary of al-Qurtubi (*al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran*) on surah 11, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿That is among the news of the unseen﴾, meaning: those are the reports. In another place it reads "that" (*dhalika*), meaning: that report and narrative is among the reports of what was hidden from you.

﴿We reveal it to you﴾, meaning: so that you may become acquainted with it.

﴿Neither you nor your people knew it﴾, meaning: they were not aware of the matter of the Flood. The Majus (Zoroastrians) now deny it. [﴿Before this﴾ is a predicate, meaning: unknown to you and to your people.]

﴿So be patient﴾ in the hardships of the message and the harm of the people, as Nuh (Noah) was patient. [from K.] And it was said: He meant their ignorance of the story of Nuh's son, even though they had heard of the matter of the Flood [in general terms]. [from W.] "So be patient," meaning: be patient, O Muhammad, in carrying out the command of God and conveying His message, and in what you encounter of harm from the disbelieving Arabs, as Nuh was patient with the harm of his people. [from K.]

﴿Indeed, the final outcome﴾ is in this world through victory, and in the Hereafter through success.

﴿Belongs to the God-conscious﴾, meaning: those who guard against shirk (associating partners with God) and sins.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud﴾**, meaning: and We sent. It is coordinated with "We sent Nuh." It was said that he is called their brother because he was one of them, since the tribe gathered them, as you say, "O brother of Tamim." It was also said that he is called their brother because he is a son of Adam as they are sons of Adam. This was discussed earlier in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 235 onward.]]. They were worshippers of idols. It was said: they are two 'Ads, the first 'Ad and the other 'Ad. Those are the first, and as for the other, it is Shaddad and Luqman, who are mentioned in His saying: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 44.]] [al-Fajr: 7]. 'Ad was the name of a man, then it continued to be applied to the people who traced their descent to him.

**(He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.")** The word "ghayruhu" is in the genitive (*khafd*) according to the wording, and "ghayruhu" in the nominative (*raf'*) according to the position, and "ghayruhu" in the accusative as an exception (*istithna'*).

**(You are nothing but fabricators.)** That is: in your taking a god other than Him, you are none but liars against Him, Majestic and Mighty.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the One who originated me.﴾** Its meaning has already been mentioned. *Al-fitrah* is the beginning of creation.

**(Will you not reason?)** [i.e., consider] what befell the people of Nuh when they denied the messengers.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And, O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance﴾** This was mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

**(He will send the sky upon you in abundance.)** It is apocopated (*jazm*) because it is a response, and it carries the sense of a conditional. **"(upon you in abundance)"** is in the accusative as a circumstantial (*hal*), and it carries the sense of profusion, meaning: He will send the sky with rain, successive, one part following another. The Arabs drop the *ha'* in *mif'al* when used as a relative adjective, and *mif'al* mostly comes from *af'ala*, but here it has come from *fa'ala*, because it is from "the sky poured forth (*darrat*) and pours (*tadirru* and *tadurru*), so it is *midrar*." The people of Hud, that is 'Ad, were people of gardens, crops, and cultivation, and their dwellings were the sands between al-Sham and Yemen, as was mentioned in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 236.]].

**(And He will add to your strength upon your strength.)** It is coordinated with "yursil" (He will send).

**(Strength upon your strength.)** Mujahid said: "Might upon your might." al-Dahhak said: "Fertility upon your fertility." Ali ibn Isa said: "Honour upon your honour." Ikrimah said: "Children upon your children." It was also said: Allah withheld rain from them and made the wombs barren for three years, so no child was born to them. Hud said to them: "If you believe, Allah will revive your lands, and grant you wealth and children; that is the strength." al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "He will add to you strength in blessings."

**(And do not turn away as criminals.)** That is: do not turn away from what I call you to, and persist in disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof."﴾** That is: a clear argument.

**(We are not going to abandon our gods on your word, and we are not believers in you.)** This is their insistence upon disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾** That is: has afflicted you.

**(Some of our gods.)** That is: our idols.

**(With evil.)** That is: with madness, because of your reviling them, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: *'arahu al-amr* and *i'taraha* when a matter befalls him. From this is His saying: ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 47.]] [al-Hajj: 36].

**(He said: "I call Allah to witness.")** That is: against myself.

**(And bear witness.)** That is: and I call you to witness, not because they were people of testimony, but it is an end to affirmation, that is, so that you may know **(that I am free of what)** that is, of worshipping the idols that you worship.

**(So scheme against me all together.)** That is: you and your idols, in your enmity and harm toward me.

**(Then give me no respite.)** That is: do not delay me. This statement, despite the multitude of enemies, indicates complete confidence in the victory of Allah, Exalted is He. It is among the signs of prophethood that the messenger alone should say to his people: "So scheme against me all together." Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said to Quraysh. And Nuh ﷺ said: ﴿So resolve upon your affair and your partners﴾ [[See vol. 8, p. 362.]] [Yunus: 71], and so on.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord.﴾** That is: I am content with His judgment, and I trust in His support.

**(There is no creature)** That is: no soul that crawls upon the earth, and it is in the nominative position as a *mubtada'* (subject).

**(But He holds its forelock.)** That is: He directs it as He wills, and restrains it from what He wills, meaning: you cannot reach my harm. Everything that has a spirit is called *dabb* and *dabbah*, and the *ha'* is for emphasis. al-Farra' said: its owner, and the one capable over it. al-Qutabi said: its subduer, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued. al-Dahhak said: He gives it life and then makes it die, and the meanings are close. The forelock is the hair at the front of the head. And *nasawtu al-rajul ansuhu naswan* means I pulled his forelock. Ibn Jurayj said: He specified the forelock only because the Arabs use this when they describe a person as humbled and submissive, and they say: "The forelock of so-and-so is only in the hand of so-and-so," meaning: he is obedient to him and he directs him as he wishes. And when they captured a prisoner and wished to release him as a favour, they would cut his forelock so that he would be known by that, as a mark of pride over him. So He addressed them with what they recognised in their speech.

al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said in *Nawadir al-Usul*, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾: its meaning, in our view, is that Allah, Exalted is He, decreed the measures of the deeds of the servants, then looked at them, then created His creatures. His sight penetrated all that they would do before He created them. When He created them, He placed the light of that gaze in their forelocks. That light holds their forelocks, directing them toward their deeds that were decreed for them on the Day of Decrees. Allah created the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. This was related by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah decreed the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." For this reason the messengers became strong and became among the *Ulu al-'Azm* (the steadfast messengers), because they perceived the light of the forelocks, and were certain that all of His creation is led by those lights toward the deeds upon which His gaze penetrated. So the one with the greatest share of this perception is the strongest in resolve. For this reason Hud, the Prophet ﷺ, was strengthened, so that he said: "So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock." The forelock is so named because the deeds have been made explicit (*nussat*) and have emerged from the unseen of the unseen, and so have become explicit in the decrees, the sight of the Creator penetrating with power into all the movements of creation. Then the movements of every living creature that crawls upon the earth were placed on its forehead between its eyes, so that place on it is called the forelock (*nasiyah*), because it makes explicit (*tanuss*) the movements of the servants by what has been decreed. So the forelock is taken from the explicit movements upon which Allah, Exalted is He, looked before He created them. He described the forelock of Abu Jahl, saying: ﴿A lying, sinning forelock﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 124.]] [al-'Alaq: 16]. It informs that the forelocks in it are lying and sinning. According to what they interpreted, it would be impossible for the forelock to be attributed to lying and sinning. [And Allah knows best.]

**(Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.)** al-Nahhas said: *al-sirat* in the language is the clear method. The meaning is that Allah, His praise be exalted, although He is capable of everything, does not seize them except with truth. It was also said: its meaning is that there is no defect in His management, and no inconsistency in His creation, glory be to Him.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away…﴾** It is in a position of apocopation (*jazm*), therefore the *nun* is dropped from it; the original is *tatawallaw*, and the *ta'* is dropped because two *ta's* came together.

**(Then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you.)** In the sense of: I have made clear to you.

**(And my Lord will replace you with another people.)** That is: He will destroy you and create one who is more obedient to Him than you, who will affirm His oneness and worship Him. "Wa yastakhlifu" is cut off from what precedes it, and therefore it is in the nominative; or it is coordinated with what must follow the *fa'* in His saying: "Then I have conveyed to you." It is narrated from Hafs from Asim: "wa yastakhlif" with apocopation, taking it as a reference to the position of the *fa'* and what follows it, like: ﴿And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-A'raf: 186] [the reading with *ba'* and sukun on the *ra'* is a reading; see vol. 7, p. 334].

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you will not harm Him at all.﴾** That is: by your turning away and your aversion.

**(Indeed, my Lord is over all things a Guardian.)** That is: a Preserver of all things. "'Ala" here has the meaning of "li" (for), so He preserves me from your reaching me with harm.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when Our command came…﴾** That is: Our punishment, with the destruction of 'Ad.

**(We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us.)** Because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah, Exalted is He, even if he has good deeds. In the Sahih of Muslim and al-Bukhari and others, from the Prophet ﷺ: "No one among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." It was also said: the meaning of "by mercy from Us" is that We made clear to them the guidance, which is itself a mercy. They were four thousand. It was also said: three thousand.

**(And We saved them from a severe punishment.)** That is: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the barren wind, as Allah mentioned in *al-Dhariyat* [[See vol. 17, p. 50.]] and elsewhere, and it will come. al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: the punishment with which the Prophet threatens his community, when it arrives, Allah saves the Prophet and the believers with him from it. Yes! It is not far-fetched that Allah tests a prophet and his people, and afflicts them with a calamity that covers them, and that this is a punishment for the disbelievers and a purification for the believers, if it is not what the Prophet threatened them with.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that was 'Ad…﴾** "'Ad" is a subject and predicate (*mubtada' wa khabar*). al-Kisa'i related that among the Arabs there are some who do not inflect "'Ad," making it the name of a tribe.

**(They denied the signs of their Lord.)** That is: they denied the miracles and rejected them.

**(And disobeyed His messengers.)** He means Hud alone, because He did not send any other messenger to them. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 127.]] [al-Mu'minun: 51], meaning the Prophet ﷺ alone, because there was no other messenger in his time. Here the plural is used because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. It was also said: they disobeyed Hud and the messengers before him, and they were such that if a thousand messengers had been sent to them, they would have denied all of them.

**(And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.)** That is: their lowly ones followed their leaders. *Al-jabbar* is the arrogant one. *Al-'anid* is the transgressor who does not accept the truth and does not submit to it [in one copy: "yanqad" (submit)]. Abu Ubayd said: *al-'anid*, *al-'anud*, *al-'ani*d, and *al-mu'anid* are the one who opposes with dissent, and from this the vein that bursts with blood is called *'anid*. The rajaz poet said:

*"Indeed I am old, I cannot bear the 'unad..."*
[The verse's first half: "When you travel, make me the middle…"]

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾** That is: it was attached to them.

**(And on the Day of Resurrection.)** That is: and on the Day of Resurrection they will be followed by the like of that. So the pause is at His saying: "And on the Day of Resurrection."

**(Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord.)** al-Farra' said: that is, they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord. He said: it is said *kafartuhu* and *kafartu bihi*, like *shakartuhu* and *shakartu lahu*.

**(Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud!)** That is: may they never cease to be far from the mercy of Allah. *Al-bu'd* is destruction, and *al-bu'd* is distance from good. It is said: *ba'uda yab'udu bu'dan* when he delayed and distanced himself, and *ba'ida yab'adu ba'adan* when he perished. He said:

*"Let not my people be far, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the misfortunes..."* [[The verse's explanation was given earlier in vol. 6, p. 14.]]

And al-Nabigha said:

*"So do not let them be far, for death is a watering place, and every man will one day be a passing shade."*

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud﴾**, meaning: and We sent. It is coordinated with "We sent Nuh." It was said that he is called their brother because he was one of them, since the tribe gathered them, as you say, "O brother of Tamim." It was also said that he is called their brother because he is a son of Adam as they are sons of Adam. This was discussed earlier in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 235 onward.]]. They were worshippers of idols. It was said: they are two 'Ads, the first 'Ad and the other 'Ad. Those are the first, and as for the other, it is Shaddad and Luqman, who are mentioned in His saying: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 44.]] [al-Fajr: 7]. 'Ad was the name of a man, then it continued to be applied to the people who traced their descent to him.

**(He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.")** The word "ghayruhu" is in the genitive (*khafd*) according to the wording, and "ghayruhu" in the nominative (*raf'*) according to the position, and "ghayruhu" in the accusative as an exception (*istithna'*).

**(You are nothing but fabricators.)** That is: in your taking a god other than Him, you are none but liars against Him, Majestic and Mighty.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the One who originated me.﴾** Its meaning has already been mentioned. *Al-fitrah* is the beginning of creation.

**(Will you not reason?)** [i.e., consider] what befell the people of Nuh when they denied the messengers.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And, O my people, ask forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance﴾** This was mentioned at the beginning of the surah.

**(He will send the sky upon you in abundance.)** It is apocopated (*jazm*) because it is a response, and it carries the sense of a conditional. **"(upon you in abundance)"** is in the accusative as a circumstantial (*hal*), and it carries the sense of profusion, meaning: He will send the sky with rain, successive, one part following another. The Arabs drop the *ha'* in *mif'al* when used as a relative adjective, and *mif'al* mostly comes from *af'ala*, but here it has come from *fa'ala*, because it is from "the sky poured forth (*darrat*) and pours (*tadirru* and *tadurru*), so it is *midrar*." The people of Hud, that is 'Ad, were people of gardens, crops, and cultivation, and their dwellings were the sands between al-Sham and Yemen, as was mentioned in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 236.]].

**(And He will add to your strength upon your strength.)** It is coordinated with "yursil" (He will send).

**(Strength upon your strength.)** Mujahid said: "Might upon your might." al-Dahhak said: "Fertility upon your fertility." Ali ibn Isa said: "Honour upon your honour." Ikrimah said: "Children upon your children." It was also said: Allah withheld rain from them and made the wombs barren for three years, so no child was born to them. Hud said to them: "If you believe, Allah will revive your lands, and grant you wealth and children; that is the strength." al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "He will add to you strength in blessings."

**(And do not turn away as criminals.)** That is: do not turn away from what I call you to, and persist in disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof."﴾** That is: a clear argument.

**(We are not going to abandon our gods on your word, and we are not believers in you.)** This is their insistence upon disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾** That is: has afflicted you.

**(Some of our gods.)** That is: our idols.

**(With evil.)** That is: with madness, because of your reviling them, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: *'arahu al-amr* and *i'taraha* when a matter befalls him. From this is His saying: ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 47.]] [al-Hajj: 36].

**(He said: "I call Allah to witness.")** That is: against myself.

**(And bear witness.)** That is: and I call you to witness, not because they were people of testimony, but it is an end to affirmation, that is, so that you may know **(that I am free of what)** that is, of worshipping the idols that you worship.

**(So scheme against me all together.)** That is: you and your idols, in your enmity and harm toward me.

**(Then give me no respite.)** That is: do not delay me. This statement, despite the multitude of enemies, indicates complete confidence in the victory of Allah, Exalted is He. It is among the signs of prophethood that the messenger alone should say to his people: "So scheme against me all together." Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said to Quraysh. And Nuh ﷺ said: ﴿So resolve upon your affair and your partners﴾ [[See vol. 8, p. 362.]] [Yunus: 71], and so on.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord.﴾** That is: I am content with His judgment, and I trust in His support.

**(There is no creature)** That is: no soul that crawls upon the earth, and it is in the nominative position as a *mubtada'* (subject).

**(But He holds its forelock.)** That is: He directs it as He wills, and restrains it from what He wills, meaning: you cannot reach my harm. Everything that has a spirit is called *dabb* and *dabbah*, and the *ha'* is for emphasis. al-Farra' said: its owner, and the one capable over it. al-Qutabi said: its subduer, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued. al-Dahhak said: He gives it life and then makes it die, and the meanings are close. The forelock is the hair at the front of the head. And *nasawtu al-rajul ansuhu naswan* means I pulled his forelock. Ibn Jurayj said: He specified the forelock only because the Arabs use this when they describe a person as humbled and submissive, and they say: "The forelock of so-and-so is only in the hand of so-and-so," meaning: he is obedient to him and he directs him as he wishes. And when they captured a prisoner and wished to release him as a favour, they would cut his forelock so that he would be known by that, as a mark of pride over him. So He addressed them with what they recognised in their speech.

al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said in *Nawadir al-Usul*, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾: its meaning, in our view, is that Allah, Exalted is He, decreed the measures of the deeds of the servants, then looked at them, then created His creatures. His sight penetrated all that they would do before He created them. When He created them, He placed the light of that gaze in their forelocks. That light holds their forelocks, directing them toward their deeds that were decreed for them on the Day of Decrees. Allah created the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. This was related by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah decreed the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." For this reason the messengers became strong and became among the *Ulu al-'Azm* (the steadfast messengers), because they perceived the light of the forelocks, and were certain that all of His creation is led by those lights toward the deeds upon which His gaze penetrated. So the one with the greatest share of this perception is the strongest in resolve. For this reason Hud, the Prophet ﷺ, was strengthened, so that he said: "So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock." The forelock is so named because the deeds have been made explicit (*nussat*) and have emerged from the unseen of the unseen, and so have become explicit in the decrees, the sight of the Creator penetrating with power into all the movements of creation. Then the movements of every living creature that crawls upon the earth were placed on its forehead between its eyes, so that place on it is called the forelock (*nasiyah*), because it makes explicit (*tanuss*) the movements of the servants by what has been decreed. So the forelock is taken from the explicit movements upon which Allah, Exalted is He, looked before He created them. He described the forelock of Abu Jahl, saying: ﴿A lying, sinning forelock﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 124.]] [al-'Alaq: 16]. It informs that the forelocks in it are lying and sinning. According to what they interpreted, it would be impossible for the forelock to be attributed to lying and sinning. [And Allah knows best.]

**(Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.)** al-Nahhas said: *al-sirat* in the language is the clear method. The meaning is that Allah, His praise be exalted, although He is capable of everything, does not seize them except with truth. It was also said: its meaning is that there is no defect in His management, and no inconsistency in His creation, glory be to Him.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away…﴾** It is in a position of apocopation (*jazm*), therefore the *nun* is dropped from it; the original is *tatawallaw*, and the *ta'* is dropped because two *ta's* came together.

**(Then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you.)** In the sense of: I have made clear to you.

**(And my Lord will replace you with another people.)** That is: He will destroy you and create one who is more obedient to Him than you, who will affirm His oneness and worship Him. "Wa yastakhlifu" is cut off from what precedes it, and therefore it is in the nominative; or it is coordinated with what must follow the *fa'* in His saying: "Then I have conveyed to you." It is narrated from Hafs from Asim: "wa yastakhlif" with apocopation, taking it as a reference to the position of the *fa'* and what follows it, like: ﴿And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-A'raf: 186] [the reading with *ba'* and sukun on the *ra'* is a reading; see vol. 7, p. 334].

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you will not harm Him at all.﴾** That is: by your turning away and your aversion.

**(Indeed, my Lord is over all things a Guardian.)** That is: a Preserver of all things. "'Ala" here has the meaning of "li" (for), so He preserves me from your reaching me with harm.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when Our command came…﴾** That is: Our punishment, with the destruction of 'Ad.

**(We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us.)** Because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah, Exalted is He, even if he has good deeds. In the Sahih of Muslim and al-Bukhari and others, from the Prophet ﷺ: "No one among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." It was also said: the meaning of "by mercy from Us" is that We made clear to them the guidance, which is itself a mercy. They were four thousand. It was also said: three thousand.

**(And We saved them from a severe punishment.)** That is: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the barren wind, as Allah mentioned in *al-Dhariyat* [[See vol. 17, p. 50.]] and elsewhere, and it will come. al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: the punishment with which the Prophet threatens his community, when it arrives, Allah saves the Prophet and the believers with him from it. Yes! It is not far-fetched that Allah tests a prophet and his people, and afflicts them with a calamity that covers them, and that this is a punishment for the disbelievers and a purification for the believers, if it is not what the Prophet threatened them with.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that was 'Ad…﴾** "'Ad" is a subject and predicate (*mubtada' wa khabar*). al-Kisa'i related that among the Arabs there are some who do not inflect "'Ad," making it the name of a tribe.

**(They denied the signs of their Lord.)** That is: they denied the miracles and rejected them.

**(And disobeyed His messengers.)** He means Hud alone, because He did not send any other messenger to them. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 127.]] [al-Mu'minun: 51], meaning the Prophet ﷺ alone, because there was no other messenger in his time. Here the plural is used because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. It was also said: they disobeyed Hud and the messengers before him, and they were such that if a thousand messengers had been sent to them, they would have denied all of them.

**(And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.)** That is: their lowly ones followed their leaders. *Al-jabbar* is the arrogant one. *Al-'anid* is the transgressor who does not accept the truth and does not submit to it [in one copy: "yanqad" (submit)]. Abu Ubayd said: *al-'anid*, *al-'anud*, *al-'ani*d, and *al-mu'anid* are the one who opposes with dissent, and from this the vein that bursts with blood is called *'anid*. The rajaz poet said:

*"Indeed I am old, I cannot bear the 'unad..."*
[The verse's first half: "When you travel, make me the middle…"]

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾** That is: it was attached to them.

**(And on the Day of Resurrection.)** That is: and on the Day of Resurrection they will be followed by the like of that. So the pause is at His saying: "And on the Day of Resurrection."

**(Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord.)** al-Farra' said: that is, they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord. He said: it is said *kafartuhu* and *kafartu bihi*, like *shakartuhu* and *shakartu lahu*.

**(Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud!)** That is: may they never cease to be far from the mercy of Allah. *Al-bu'd* is destruction, and *al-bu'd* is distance from good. It is said: *ba'uda yab'udu bu'dan* when he delayed and distanced himself, and *ba'ida yab'adu ba'adan* when he perished. He said:

*"Let not my people be far, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the misfortunes..."* [[The verse's explanation was given earlier in vol. 6, p. 14.]]

And al-Nabigha said:

*"So do not let them be far, for death is a watering place, and every man will one day be a passing shade."*

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud﴾**, meaning: and We sent. It is coordinated with "We sent Nuh." It was said that he is called their brother because he was one of them, since the tribe gathered them, as you say, "O brother of Tamim." It was also said that he is called their brother because he is a son of Adam as they are sons of Adam. This was discussed earlier in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 235 onward.]]. They were worshippers of idols. It was said: they are two 'Ads, the first 'Ad and the other 'Ad. Those are the first, and as for the other, it is Shaddad and Luqman, who are mentioned in His saying: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 44.]] [al-Fajr: 7]. 'Ad was the name of a man, then it continued to be applied to the people who traced their descent to him.

**(You are nothing but fabricators.)** That is: in your taking a god other than Him, you are none but liars against Him, Majestic and Mighty.

**(Will you not reason?)** [i.e., consider] what befell the people of Nuh when they denied the messengers.

The Arabs drop the *ha'* in *mif'al* when used as a relative adjective, and *mif'al* mostly comes from *af'ala*, but here it has come from *fa'ala*, because it is from "the sky poured forth (*darrat*) and pours (*tadirru* and *tadurru*), so it is *midrar*." The people of Hud, that is 'Ad, were people of gardens, crops, and cultivation, and their dwellings were the sands between al-Sham and Yemen, as was mentioned in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 236.]].

**(And He will add to your strength upon your strength.)** It is coordinated with "yursil" (He will send).

**(Strength upon your strength.)** Mujahid said: "Might upon your might." al-Dahhak said: "Fertility upon your fertility." Ali ibn Isa said: "Honour upon your honour." Ikrimah said: "Children upon your children." It was also said: Allah withheld rain from them and made the wombs barren for three years, so no child was born to them. Hud said to them: "If you believe, Allah will revive your lands, and grant you wealth and children; that is the strength." al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "He will add to you strength in blessings."

**(And do not turn away as criminals.)** That is: do not turn away from what I call you to, and persist in disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof."﴾** That is: a clear argument.

**(We are not going to abandon our gods on your word, and we are not believers in you.)** This is their insistence upon disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾** That is: has afflicted you.

**(Some of our gods.)** That is: our idols.

**(With evil.)** That is: with madness, because of your reviling them, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: *'arahu al-amr* and *i'taraha* when a matter befalls him. From this is His saying: ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 47.]] [al-Hajj: 36].

**(He said: "I call Allah to witness.")** That is: against myself.

**(And bear witness.)** That is: and I call you to witness, not because they were people of testimony, but it is an end to affirmation, that is, so that you may know **(that I am free of what)** that is, of worshipping the idols that you worship.

**(So scheme against me all together.)** That is: you and your idols, in your enmity and harm toward me.

**(Then give me no respite.)** That is: do not delay me. This statement, despite the multitude of enemies, indicates complete confidence in the victory of Allah, Exalted is He. It is among the signs of prophethood that the messenger alone should say to his people: "So scheme against me all together." Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said to Quraysh. And Nuh ﷺ said: ﴿So resolve upon your affair and your partners﴾ [[See vol. 8, p. 362.]] [Yunus: 71], and so on.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord.﴾** That is: I am content with His judgment, and I trust in His support.

**(There is no creature)** That is: no soul that crawls upon the earth, and it is in the nominative position as a *mubtada'* (subject).

**(But He holds its forelock.)** That is: He directs it as He wills, and restrains it from what He wills, meaning: you cannot reach my harm. Everything that has a spirit is called *dabb* and *dabbah*, and the *ha'* is for emphasis. al-Farra' said: its owner, and the one capable over it. al-Qutabi said: its subduer, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued. al-Dahhak said: He gives it life and then makes it die, and the meanings are close. The forelock is the hair at the front of the head. And *nasawtu al-rajul ansuhu naswan* means I pulled his forelock. Ibn Jurayj said: He specified the forelock only because the Arabs use this when they describe a person as humbled and submissive, and they say: "The forelock of so-and-so is only in the hand of so-and-so," meaning: he is obedient to him and he directs him as he wishes. And when they captured a prisoner and wished to release him as a favour, they would cut his forelock so that he would be known by that, as a mark of pride over him. So He addressed them with what they recognised in their speech.

al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said in *Nawadir al-Usul*, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾: its meaning, in our view, is that Allah, Exalted is He, decreed the measures of the deeds of the servants, then looked at them, then created His creatures. His sight penetrated all that they would do before He created them. When He created them, He placed the light of that gaze in their forelocks. That light holds their forelocks, directing them toward their deeds that were decreed for them on the Day of Decrees. Allah created the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. This was related by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah decreed the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." For this reason the messengers became strong and became among the *Ulu al-'Azm* (the steadfast messengers), because they perceived the light of the forelocks, and were certain that all of His creation is led by those lights toward the deeds upon which His gaze penetrated. So the one with the greatest share of this perception is the strongest in resolve. For this reason Hud, the Prophet ﷺ, was strengthened, so that he said: "So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock." The forelock is so named because the deeds have been made explicit (*nussat*) and have emerged from the unseen of the unseen, and so have become explicit in the decrees, the sight of the Creator penetrating with power into all the movements of creation. Then the movements of every living creature that crawls upon the earth were placed on its forehead between its eyes, so that place on it is called the forelock (*nasiyah*), because it makes explicit (*tanuss*) the movements of the servants by what has been decreed. So the forelock is taken from the explicit movements upon which Allah, Exalted is He, looked before He created them. He described the forelock of Abu Jahl, saying: ﴿A lying, sinning forelock﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 124.]] [al-'Alaq: 16]. It informs that the forelocks in it are lying and sinning. According to what they interpreted, it would be impossible for the forelock to be attributed to lying and sinning. [And Allah knows best.]

**(Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.)** al-Nahhas said: *al-sirat* in the language is the clear method. The meaning is that Allah, His praise be exalted, although He is capable of everything, does not seize them except with truth. It was also said: its meaning is that there is no defect in His management, and no inconsistency in His creation, glory be to Him.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away…﴾** It is in a position of apocopation (*jazm*), therefore the *nun* is dropped from it; the original is *tatawallaw*, and the *ta'* is dropped because two *ta's* came together.

**(Then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you.)** In the sense of: I have made clear to you.

**(And my Lord will replace you with another people.)** That is: He will destroy you and create one who is more obedient to Him than you, who will affirm His oneness and worship Him. "Wa yastakhlifu" is cut off from what precedes it, and therefore it is in the nominative; or it is coordinated with what must follow the *fa'* in His saying: "Then I have conveyed to you." It is narrated from Hafs from Asim: "wa yastakhlif" with apocopation, taking it as a reference to the position of the *fa'* and what follows it, like: ﴿And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-A'raf: 186] [the reading with *ba'* and sukun on the *ra'* is a reading; see vol. 7, p. 334].

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you will not harm Him at all.﴾** That is: by your turning away and your aversion.

**(Indeed, my Lord is over all things a Guardian.)** That is: a Preserver of all things. "'Ala" here has the meaning of "li" (for), so He preserves me from your reaching me with harm.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when Our command came…﴾** That is: Our punishment, with the destruction of 'Ad.

**(We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us.)** Because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah, Exalted is He, even if he has good deeds. In the Sahih of Muslim and al-Bukhari and others, from the Prophet ﷺ: "No one among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." It was also said: the meaning of "by mercy from Us" is that We made clear to them the guidance, which is itself a mercy. They were four thousand. It was also said: three thousand.

**(And We saved them from a severe punishment.)** That is: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the barren wind, as Allah mentioned in *al-Dhariyat* [[See vol. 17, p. 50.]] and elsewhere, and it will come. al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: the punishment with which the Prophet threatens his community, when it arrives, Allah saves the Prophet and the believers with him from it. Yes! It is not far-fetched that Allah tests a prophet and his people, and afflicts them with a calamity that covers them, and that this is a punishment for the disbelievers and a purification for the believers, if it is not what the Prophet threatened them with.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that was 'Ad…﴾** "'Ad" is a subject and predicate (*mubtada' wa khabar*). al-Kisa'i related that among the Arabs there are some who do not inflect "'Ad," making it the name of a tribe.

**(They denied the signs of their Lord.)** That is: they denied the miracles and rejected them.

**(And disobeyed His messengers.)** He means Hud alone, because He did not send any other messenger to them. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 127.]] [al-Mu'minun: 51], meaning the Prophet ﷺ alone, because there was no other messenger in his time. Here the plural is used because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. It was also said: they disobeyed Hud and the messengers before him, and they were such that if a thousand messengers had been sent to them, they would have denied all of them.

**(And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.)** That is: their lowly ones followed their leaders. *Al-jabbar* is the arrogant one. *Al-'anid* is the transgressor who does not accept the truth and does not submit to it [in one copy: "yanqad" (submit)]. Abu Ubayd said: *al-'anid*, *al-'anud*, *al-'ani*d, and *al-mu'anid* are the one who opposes with dissent, and from this the vein that bursts with blood is called *'anid*. The rajaz poet said:

*"Indeed I am old, I cannot bear the 'unad..."*
[The verse's first half: "When you travel, make me the middle…"]

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾** That is: it was attached to them.

**(And on the Day of Resurrection.)** That is: and on the Day of Resurrection they will be followed by the like of that. So the pause is at His saying: "And on the Day of Resurrection."

**(Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord.)** al-Farra' said: that is, they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord. He said: it is said *kafartuhu* and *kafartu bihi*, like *shakartuhu* and *shakartu lahu*.

**(Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud!)** That is: may they never cease to be far from the mercy of Allah. *Al-bu'd* is destruction, and *al-bu'd* is distance from good. It is said: *ba'uda yab'udu bu'dan* when he delayed and distanced himself, and *ba'ida yab'adu ba'adan* when he perished. He said:

*"Let not my people be far, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the misfortunes..."* [[The verse's explanation was given earlier in vol. 6, p. 14.]]

And al-Nabigha said:

*"So do not let them be far, for death is a watering place, and every man will one day be a passing shade."*

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud﴾**, meaning: and We sent. It is coordinated with "We sent Nuh." It was said that he is called their brother because he was one of them, since the tribe gathered them, as you say, "O brother of Tamim." It was also said that he is called their brother because he is a son of Adam as they are sons of Adam. This was discussed earlier in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 235 onward.]]. They were worshippers of idols. It was said: they are two 'Ads, the first 'Ad and the other 'Ad. Those are the first, and as for the other, it is Shaddad and Luqman, who are mentioned in His saying: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 44.]] [al-Fajr: 7]. 'Ad was the name of a man, then it continued to be applied to the people who traced their descent to him.

**(He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him.")** The word "ghayruhu" is in the genitive (*khafd*) according to the wording, and "ghayruhu" in the nominative (*raf'*) according to the position, and "ghayruhu" in the accusative as an exception (*istithna'*).

**(You are nothing but fabricators.)** That is: in your taking a god other than Him, you are none but liars against Him, Majestic and Mighty.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the One who originated me.﴾** Its meaning has already been mentioned. *Al-fitrah* is the beginning of creation.

**(Will you not reason?)** [i.e., consider] what befell the people of Nuh when they denied the messengers.

**(He will send the sky upon you in abundance.)** It is apocopated (*jazm*) because it is a response, and it carries the sense of a conditional. **"(upon you in abundance)"** is in the accusative as a circumstantial (*hal*), and it carries the sense of profusion, meaning: He will send the sky with rain, successive, one part following another. The Arabs drop the *ha'* in *mif'al* when used as a relative adjective, and *mif'al* mostly comes from *af'ala*, but here it has come from *fa'ala*, because it is from "the sky poured forth (*darrat*) and pours (*tadirru* and *tadurru*), so it is *midrar*." The people of Hud, that is 'Ad, were people of gardens, crops, and cultivation, and their dwellings were the sands between al-Sham and Yemen, as was mentioned in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 236.]].

**(And He will add to your strength upon your strength.)** It is coordinated with "yursil" (He will send).

**(Strength upon your strength.)** Mujahid said: "Might upon your might." al-Dahhak said: "Fertility upon your fertility." Ali ibn Isa said: "Honour upon your honour." Ikrimah said: "Children upon your children." It was also said: Allah withheld rain from them and made the wombs barren for three years, so no child was born to them. Hud said to them: "If you believe, Allah will revive your lands, and grant you wealth and children; that is the strength." al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "He will add to you strength in blessings."

**(And do not turn away as criminals.)** That is: do not turn away from what I call you to, and persist in disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof."﴾** That is: a clear argument.

**(We are not going to abandon our gods on your word, and we are not believers in you.)** This is their insistence upon disbelief.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿We say only that some of our gods have struck you with evil.﴾** That is: has afflicted you.

**(Some of our gods.)** That is: our idols.

**(With evil.)** That is: with madness, because of your reviling them, according to Ibn Abbas and others. It is said: *'arahu al-amr* and *i'taraha* when a matter befalls him. From this is His saying: ﴿And feed the contented and the beggar﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 47.]] [al-Hajj: 36].

**(He said: "I call Allah to witness.")** That is: against myself.

**(And bear witness.)** That is: and I call you to witness, not because they were people of testimony, but it is an end to affirmation, that is, so that you may know **(that I am free of what)** that is, of worshipping the idols that you worship.

**(So scheme against me all together.)** That is: you and your idols, in your enmity and harm toward me.

**(Then give me no respite.)** That is: do not delay me. This statement, despite the multitude of enemies, indicates complete confidence in the victory of Allah, Exalted is He. It is among the signs of prophethood that the messenger alone should say to his people: "So scheme against me all together." Likewise the Prophet ﷺ said to Quraysh. And Nuh ﷺ said: ﴿So resolve upon your affair and your partners﴾ [[See vol. 8, p. 362.]] [Yunus: 71], and so on.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord.﴾** That is: I am content with His judgment, and I trust in His support.

**(There is no creature)** That is: no soul that crawls upon the earth, and it is in the nominative position as a *mubtada'* (subject).

**(But He holds its forelock.)** That is: He directs it as He wills, and restrains it from what He wills, meaning: you cannot reach my harm. Everything that has a spirit is called *dabb* and *dabbah*, and the *ha'* is for emphasis. al-Farra' said: its owner, and the one capable over it. al-Qutabi said: its subduer, because whoever you take by the forelock, you have subdued. al-Dahhak said: He gives it life and then makes it die, and the meanings are close. The forelock is the hair at the front of the head. And *nasawtu al-rajul ansuhu naswan* means I pulled his forelock. Ibn Jurayj said: He specified the forelock only because the Arabs use this when they describe a person as humbled and submissive, and they say: "The forelock of so-and-so is only in the hand of so-and-so," meaning: he is obedient to him and he directs him as he wishes. And when they captured a prisoner and wished to release him as a favour, they would cut his forelock so that he would be known by that, as a mark of pride over him. So He addressed them with what they recognised in their speech.

al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim said in *Nawadir al-Usul*, concerning His saying: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock﴾: its meaning, in our view, is that Allah, Exalted is He, decreed the measures of the deeds of the servants, then looked at them, then created His creatures. His sight penetrated all that they would do before He created them. When He created them, He placed the light of that gaze in their forelocks. That light holds their forelocks, directing them toward their deeds that were decreed for them on the Day of Decrees. Allah created the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth. This was related by Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Allah decreed the decrees fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." For this reason the messengers became strong and became among the *Ulu al-'Azm* (the steadfast messengers), because they perceived the light of the forelocks, and were certain that all of His creation is led by those lights toward the deeds upon which His gaze penetrated. So the one with the greatest share of this perception is the strongest in resolve. For this reason Hud, the Prophet ﷺ, was strengthened, so that he said: "So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite. Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock." The forelock is so named because the deeds have been made explicit (*nussat*) and have emerged from the unseen of the unseen, and so have become explicit in the decrees, the sight of the Creator penetrating with power into all the movements of creation. Then the movements of every living creature that crawls upon the earth were placed on its forehead between its eyes, so that place on it is called the forelock (*nasiyah*), because it makes explicit (*tanuss*) the movements of the servants by what has been decreed. So the forelock is taken from the explicit movements upon which Allah, Exalted is He, looked before He created them. He described the forelock of Abu Jahl, saying: ﴿A lying, sinning forelock﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 124.]] [al-'Alaq: 16]. It informs that the forelocks in it are lying and sinning. According to what they interpreted, it would be impossible for the forelock to be attributed to lying and sinning. [And Allah knows best.]

**(Indeed, my Lord is upon a straight path.)** al-Nahhas said: *al-sirat* in the language is the clear method. The meaning is that Allah, His praise be exalted, although He is capable of everything, does not seize them except with truth. It was also said: its meaning is that there is no defect in His management, and no inconsistency in His creation, glory be to Him.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they turn away…﴾** It is in a position of apocopation (*jazm*), therefore the *nun* is dropped from it; the original is *tatawallaw*, and the *ta'* is dropped because two *ta's* came together.

**(Then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you.)** In the sense of: I have made clear to you.

**(And my Lord will replace you with another people.)** That is: He will destroy you and create one who is more obedient to Him than you, who will affirm His oneness and worship Him. "Wa yastakhlifu" is cut off from what precedes it, and therefore it is in the nominative; or it is coordinated with what must follow the *fa'* in His saying: "Then I have conveyed to you." It is narrated from Hafs from Asim: "wa yastakhlif" with apocopation, taking it as a reference to the position of the *fa'* and what follows it, like: ﴿And He leaves them in their transgression, wandering blindly﴾ [al-A'raf: 186] [the reading with *ba'* and sukun on the *ra'* is a reading; see vol. 7, p. 334].

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And you will not harm Him at all.﴾** That is: by your turning away and your aversion.

**(Indeed, my Lord is over all things a Guardian.)** That is: a Preserver of all things. "'Ala" here has the meaning of "li" (for), so He preserves me from your reaching me with harm.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And when Our command came…﴾** That is: Our punishment, with the destruction of 'Ad.

**(We saved Hud and those who believed with him by mercy from Us.)** Because no one is saved except by the mercy of Allah, Exalted is He, even if he has good deeds. In the Sahih of Muslim and al-Bukhari and others, from the Prophet ﷺ: "No one among you will be saved by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy." It was also said: the meaning of "by mercy from Us" is that We made clear to them the guidance, which is itself a mercy. They were four thousand. It was also said: three thousand.

**(And We saved them from a severe punishment.)** That is: the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. It was also said: it is the barren wind, as Allah mentioned in *al-Dhariyat* [[See vol. 17, p. 50.]] and elsewhere, and it will come. al-Qushayri Abu Nasr said: the punishment with which the Prophet threatens his community, when it arrives, Allah saves the Prophet and the believers with him from it. Yes! It is not far-fetched that Allah tests a prophet and his people, and afflicts them with a calamity that covers them, and that this is a punishment for the disbelievers and a purification for the believers, if it is not what the Prophet threatened them with.

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that was 'Ad…﴾** "'Ad" is a subject and predicate (*mubtada' wa khabar*). al-Kisa'i related that among the Arabs there are some who do not inflect "'Ad," making it the name of a tribe.

**(They denied the signs of their Lord.)** That is: they denied the miracles and rejected them.

**(And disobeyed His messengers.)** He means Hud alone, because He did not send any other messenger to them. A parallel to this is His saying: ﴿O messengers, eat of the good things﴾ [[See vol. 12, p. 127.]] [al-Mu'minun: 51], meaning the Prophet ﷺ alone, because there was no other messenger in his time. Here the plural is used because whoever denies one messenger has disbelieved in all the messengers. It was also said: they disobeyed Hud and the messengers before him, and they were such that if a thousand messengers had been sent to them, they would have denied all of them.

**(And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.)** That is: their lowly ones followed their leaders. *Al-jabbar* is the arrogant one. *Al-'anid* is the transgressor who does not accept the truth and does not submit to it [in one copy: "yanqad" (submit)]. Abu Ubayd said: *al-'anid*, *al-'anud*, *al-'ani*d, and *al-mu'anid* are the one who opposes with dissent, and from this the vein that bursts with blood is called *'anid*. The rajaz poet said:

*"Indeed I am old, I cannot bear the 'unad..."*
[The verse's first half: "When you travel, make me the middle…"]

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse﴾** That is: it was attached to them.

**(And on the Day of Resurrection.)** That is: and on the Day of Resurrection they will be followed by the like of that. So the pause is at His saying: "And on the Day of Resurrection."

**(Unquestionably, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord.)** al-Farra' said: that is, they disbelieved the blessing of their Lord. He said: it is said *kafartuhu* and *kafartu bihi*, like *shakartuhu* and *shakartu lahu*.

**(Unquestionably, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud!)** That is: may they never cease to be far from the mercy of Allah. *Al-bu'd* is destruction, and *al-bu'd* is distance from good. It is said: *ba'uda yab'udu bu'dan* when he delayed and distanced himself, and *ba'ida yab'adu ba'adan* when he perished. He said:

*"Let not my people be far, those who are the poison of enemies and the calamity of the misfortunes..."* [[The verse's explanation was given earlier in vol. 6, p. 14.]]

And al-Nabigha said:

*"So do not let them be far, for death is a watering place, and every man will one day be a passing shade."*

**His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And to 'Ad [We sent] their brother Hud﴾**, meaning: and We sent. It is coordinated with "We sent Nuh." It was said that he is called their brother because he was one of them, since the tribe gathered them, as you say, "O brother of Tamim." It was also said that he is called their brother because he is a son of Adam as they are sons of Adam. This was discussed earlier in *al-A'raf* [[See vol. 7, p. 235 onward.]]. They were worshippers of idols. It was said: they are two 'Ads, the first 'Ad and the other 'Ad. Those are the first, and as for the other, it is Shaddad and Luqman, who are mentioned in His saying: ﴿Iram of the pillars﴾ [[See vol. 20, p. 44.]] [al-Fajr: 7]. 'Ad was the name of a man, then it continued to be applied to the people who traced their descent to him.

**(You are nothing but fabricators.)** That is: in your taking a god other than Him, you are none but liars against Him, Majestic and Mighty.
